root_causes.title: No combo executor: the shim treats 'assembled' as done, casts only spells from hand, and never makes a loop's activations, target choices or stop decision
symptoms: combos: lines get assembled and then are never fired; the sim wins by combat around round 12-13, while humans win with a loop around round 5
play_logic: engines sit on the board for 15-20 player-turns; loops stop after 1-30 activations; open-ended loops run to the 900 s clock and are scored as draws
tutoring: tutored engine pieces produce nothing once found, so tutoring looks useless
root_causes.mechanism: A line reaches the shim as a set of card names. The shim pursues it only until every piece is owned, then hands control back to stock Forge (PlanPlayerController.java:1068 'assembled, done here'). Its only action is to cast a spell from hand (castableSpell :1251 `if (!sa.isSpell()) continue;`, comboPriority walks only ZoneType.Hand at :1124). It never activates an ability, never picks a target, never casts from the graveyard, and has no stop condition or payoff step. Stock Forge scores each ability and target on its own, with no idea that the pieces form a loop. Forge does activate these cards, but aimlessly: loops that need the same target choice on every pass never start, and repeat loops stop once one more activation looks locally worthless. Only lines that finish by casting a spell (Consultation into Oracle) convert, because there the shim fires the last piece itself.
evidence: Code: PlanPlayerController.java:1068, :1124, :1251; DeckPlan.java:208-213 reads only 'cards'. No public decision hook for targets is overridden (the shim overrides 9 of about 120 PlayerControllerAi methods).

Line-completing casts across 6 plan-seat run sets: 167 permanent completions led to 5 same-turn wins (3.0%) and a 25.7% overall win rate (the 4-seat baseline); 49 spell completions led to 25 wins, 24 of them the same turn (verify/conv).

Only 18 of 235 deck-line pairs (10 of 122 unique piece sets) can be driven by casting spells from hand. 142/235 need a non-mana activated ability, 176 need an outlet, 126 carry a prerequisite (verify/lines_exec).

Wrong target on every pass: Kiki-Jiki copied Zealous Conscripts 8 times and the copy's trigger untapped Kiki 0/8 (it untapped Rionya, Mirage Phalanx or Bartz instead). After Gaea's Cradle was tapped, an Emiel blink of Derevi untapped Cradle 0/216 times. Bytecode: ControlGainAi picks opponents' permanents; TapOrUntapAi reuses tap-the-opponent logic.

Aimless loops (seat-turns with 5 or more activations, then same-turn wins): Emiel 1/37, Staff of Domination 2/17, Clock of Omens 4/27, Brain Freeze recast 3+ times 0/62. Where the byproduct is combat, loops do finish: Godo+Helm 59 same-turn wins (28/32 once Helm is actually on Godo), Magda treasure engine 35/70.
Funnel on the 3 agent_viability arms: plan seats assemble 191/384 (49.7%) against stock 236/1152 (20.5%), yet win share is 21.9% vs 22.6%. Genuine executions are about 25-32 of 191.
Humans: 10 of 12 video wins were loops executed on the turn the last piece landed; human mean win round 5.0 against stock 12.7 (recomputed in winner-own-turn units).
Convert-on-assembly upper bound for agent093: mean win round 13.1 -> 8.8 over all lines, or 10.4 counting kill-clause lines only. Assembly speed is the other half of the gap.
root_causes.already_tried: Stage 5 (54eb2f6, 2026-08-01) designed pursuit up to assembly and then 'hand back to stock'. A18/A19 (02e4451, 08-24) made the tutor gate and exempted loop triggers from the triggerMiss roll. 0.9.3 (37a08a3, 08-29) added the piece-casting veto. Conversion was named the binding gap on 08-24 (human_ceiling RESULTS), 08-26 (agent_viability RESULTS, commit 6171ef4 'conversion becomes the wall'). No conversion task was ever written; 0 of 23 shim commits execute a line. Forge's lookahead was never used in a study. The one scratch experiment in this investigation (setUseSimulation on, 2 games) crashed once (GameCopier 'Couldn't map Goblin Token') and timed out once (585 of 915 s inside simulation, one decision took 361 s).
root_causes.leverage: Thin shim mechanism plus data. Python compiles each executable line into a step script: ordered actions (cast X, activate Y targeting Z, repeat until N or a condition, then the outlet W), zones, prerequisites, stop condition. The shim interprets it with public Forge APIs. Activations: return the named non-mana SpellAbility from chooseSpellAbilityToPlay after canPlay() and ComputerUtilCost.canPayCost(); activation targets can be set in the same override. Stack-trigger targets: chooseTargetsFor is reached only when the ability has a TargetingPlayer param, so the hook is orderAndPlaySimultaneousSa (set targets, then ComputerUtil.playStack). That replaces super rather than calling it first, so it needs a thin-adapter review. Iteration cap: decline the optional loop trigger in confirmTrigger once the cap is reached. Forge public API: GameSimulator.simulateSpellAbility as a bounded, try/catch-wrapped check that a planned line finishes. Not as the pilot (2/2 experimental games failed).
root_causes.unknowns: No thin interpreter has been prototyped, so how much conversion or win rate it buys is unmeasured. Open questions: whether overriding orderAndPlaySimultaneousSa reliably captures loop triggers and still counts as a thin adapter; whether Forge's per-API sub-choosers behave once a SpellAbility is forced; how reliably free-English Spellbook descriptions compile into structured steps; CPU cost per turn. Also, stock opponents leave 61-69% of assembled lines untouched for a round (unverified), so fixing conversion alone may make the sim overrate combo decks.

root_causes.title: The plan ships Spellbook's whole catalogue as flat card sets: no win-versus-engine split, no named outlet, no order or zone, no executability filter
symptoms: combos: the AI chases engines (infinite mana, ETB, blink) as if they were kills, and 7 of 32 cEDH decks carry no win line at all
tutoring: about 70% of combo casts and tutor targets go to engine-only pieces; the outlets that would finish the engines are valued at 1 and never fetched
combos: human win lines are missing their finisher (Derevi needs Nadu plus Blind Obedience; Sisay needs Deadpool; Cabbage needs Walking Ballista)
root_causes.mechanism: combos._slim keeps card names, produces and some text, and throws away zoneLocations, template requirements and easyPrerequisites. deck_plan.py:295-301 then turns every 'included' Spellbook variant into a line: sorted by piece count, with no cap, no dedupe and no filter on what it produces. The shim reads only the names (DeckPlan.java:208), so an infinite-mana engine and a real kill look identical. Spellbook expects the player to pair an engine with a payoff. Nothing in the plan does that pairing, and the payoff card in the deck gets search value 1.
evidence: Code: deck_plan.py:295-301; combos.py:90-101; DeckPlan.java:208-213 ('produces' appears only in a comment at :28).

Shipped plans (runs_agent_shipping/plans): 168 of 238 lines (71%) produce no win under a lenient definition (which counts infinite combat, hasty tokens and opponent mill). Only 17/238 literally say 'Win the game', and 16 of those are Oracle + Consultation/Pact/Hermit Druid. 7/32 decks have no win line: derevi, nadu, dexter_kinnan, isaac_yisan, matt_sisay, kinnan, natalie_magda.

Of 173 'non-win' lines, 111 are one outlet short and that outlet is already in the deck. Thrasios, Finale of Devastation, Walking Ballista and Grapeshot sit at search value 1, and tutor_steer picked them 0 times in about 2,100 plan searches.
Effort goes to engines: 276/385 combo_casts, 288/426 tutor_cast targets and 529/866 tutor_steer picks hit pieces that appear only in resource lines (pooled over 4 arms).

Assembled engine lines win at baseline: 36/143 plan seat-games (25%). Assembled win or combat lines: 29/58 (50%). Nothing assembled: 47/311 (15%). Games ran a median of 15.5-20 player-turns after the first engine line assembled.
Dead lines kept: Tainted Pact + Oracle is in 8 decks, but Tainted Pact exiled at most 1 card in 168 of 168 resolutions. isaac_yisan ships 29 lines; there are 3 exact duplicates.

Human acceptance check: of 11 human combo wins, 5 are present as lines. 3 clearly lack an outlet the deck contains. The rest fail on decklist fidelity (Rog/Thras is missing Six; Kinnan is the wrong build) or have no label (Magda g1).
root_causes.already_tried: engine/combos.py has one commit ever (0834ece, 2026-07-31); the line source has never been revised. For precons, a 'synergy lines' fallback was built on the false 'zero variants' premise. It made prediction worse (rho 0.255 -> 0.142) and was not shipped. No produces filter has ever existed.
root_causes.leverage: Data only (Python, deck_plan.py/combos.py). Keep the full Spellbook variant. Classify each variant as win, engine or lock, treating infinite combat phases, infinite hasty tokens and infinite power as wins. Compose engine lines with an outlet already in the deck, and give outlets real search value. Emit order, zone and a final-piece flag per piece, plus prerequisites and a stop condition. Drop or mark Tainted Pact + Oracle and RemoveDeck-blocked lines. Cap and dedupe lines. Use the labelled human win lines as the acceptance set. Hazard: under today's shim, adding Thassa's Oracle as a line piece would get it cast early and 'assembled'. Outlet data must ship together with sequencing and the executor (RC1, RC7).
root_causes.unknowns: No simulation measured the win-rate effect of rebuilt lines. The 71% figure depends on the classifier (71% lenient, 93% strict). The outlet list is hand-picked (126/168 or 107/168 matched by type; the investigator's 151 was not reproducible). Whether Spellbook's feature/template graph supports automatic outlet composition is unchecked.

root_causes.title: Forge's AI hard-excludes every card scripted AI:RemoveDeck:All, which blocks cEDH combo pieces, some tutors and about 12% of cEDH nonland cards, for opponents too
symptoms: play_logic: stock seats hold about 2.3 dead cards per cEDH game; about 3 nonland cards per precon deck are never cast (Signets, Beast Within, Toxic Deluge); one precon commander (Winter, Cynical Opportunist) is never cast

combos: engines built on flagged activated abilities (printed Clock of Omens, Devoted Druid, Quirion/Scryb Ranger, Aphetto Alchemist) are never activated by any seat; stock never casts Demonic Consultation
tutoring: stock never casts Vampiric Tutor, Summoner's Pact, Diabolic Intent
measurement: stock 'opponents' never cast Consultation, LED, Ad Nauseam, Doomsday or Vampiric, so the cEDH gauntlet is weaker than its decklists
root_causes.mechanism: AiController.getSpellAbilityToPlay runs saList.removeIf on every spell or ability whose host card's own script carries AI:RemoveDeck:All, and the priority comparator subtracts 10 for them. The removal is unconditional (no profile switch). Only the counterspell pre-pass, ETB counters, PlayBeforeLandDrop and copies of flagged cards escape it. The shim's castableSpell checks only canPlay/canPayCost, so it rescues flagged SPELLS that are in plan lines or tutor lists. It never offers activated abilities, so flagged engines stay dead.
evidence: Bytecode (javap, 2.0.13): AiController.getSpellAbilityToPlay offsets 258-264 removeIf(lambda$getSpellAbilityToPlay$8 = isLandAbility() || ComputerUtilCard.isCardRemAIDeck(host)); saComparator offsets 122-128 give -10. canPlaySa and SpellAbilityPicker never read the flag.

Stock cEDH seats cast 178/3430 (5.2%) of the flagged nonland cards they drew; 175 of those were counterspells cast through the unfiltered pre-pass. Unflagged: 11110/17604 (63.1%). Control group of RemoveDeck:Random cards, which are not filtered: 2727/3914 (69.7%). Precon stock: 24/2570 (0.9%) vs 71.8%.

Natural experiment with activations: printed flagged permanents 1/459; copies of the same cards 10/16. Printed Clock of Omens 0 activations in 135 battlefield entries, against 344 activations by Sculpting Steel, Metamorph and Impersonator copies.
Demonic Consultation: 0 stock casts in 69+ seat-games holding it; 51 plan casts through the shim. Thassa's Oracle cast by stock in 138 seat-games, 0 Oracle wins.

Scope: 91/238 cEDH lines (25/32 decks) contain a flagged piece. 52 are hard-blocked for both seat types (flagged non-mana activation), 10 only for stock (cast-only piece), 29 have only mana abilities flagged. Flagged cards are 12.1% of cEDH nonland cards (285/2362; rograkh_silas 22.1%). Unflagged: Oracle, Tainted Pact, Breach, Kiki-Jiki, Heliod, Ballista, Dramatic Reversal, Portal.
Plan seats cast 24.6% of flagged cards they hold, and 5.6% on precons (93 of 133 precon flagged casts were incidental instant_hold substitutions).

Inherited follow-on errors (unverified): 30% of stock classic rituals wasted, with a flagged card in hand in 51/51 reconstructed cases; stock discards line pieces or tutors at cleanup 0.27 times per seat-game; about 10% of precon turns end with a castable permanent unspent, about half of them flagged-only.
root_causes.already_tried: Nothing. No repo file, doc, test or study mentions RemoveDeck or isCardRemAIDeck. The shim's spell rescue is incidental to combo_cast/tutor_cast.
root_causes.leverage: Thin shim mechanism plus data. After super.chooseSpellAbilityToPlay, collect the plan seat's flagged SpellAbilities that plan data names, including non-mana activated abilities. Evaluate each with the public getAi().canPlaySa() (unfiltered) and take it when it passes and plan timing data allows. Cards flagged because Forge's per-API logic is weak (Consultation NameCard, Ad Nauseam, Final Fortune, Pacts) need timing preconditions as data or they will fire suicidally. Decide explicitly whether opponent seats also get readmission (realistic opponents versus a stock baseline). Do not edit res/ card scripts. Product: list flagged cards per deck (from cardsfolder.zip or Deck.getUnplayableAICards) and keep them out of 'cold' and cut verdicts.
root_causes.unknowns: Whether readmitted cards are played sensibly: no sim has tested canPlaySa-driven readmission. The win-rate cost of the dead cards (paired A/B needed). Whether flagged mana abilities are usable in payment: LED shows 0 MANA uses. How stock seats activated a Clock 32 times, possibly through the cost-payment path. The ritual-waste link is inferred, not read from ManaAi source.

root_causes.title: Tutor targets are valued by Spellbook membership and keyword regex, not by what this pilot can convert, and combo steering has absolute priority
symptoms: tutoring: plan Magda discards stock Forge's Portal to Phyrexia pick every time and wins half as often
tutoring: engines, draw engines and real outlets sit at value 1, so early tutors never fetch an engine (humans do so half the time)
play_logic: 'loses the game' drawback text scores as a finisher, so plan seats fetch Pact of Negation and lose to their own Pacts and Final Fortunes
root_causes.mechanism: deck_plan.py:375-393 gives value 8 to any piece of any Spellbook line, and to any card matching the finisher regex ('loses? the game', 'combat damage to a player'). Big bombs get 6; engines and most outlets get 1. In the shim, a sighted line's missing piece wins outright (PlanPlayerController.java:1792), and a plan pick wins whenever its value is strictly higher (:1803). So any engine piece beats a proven finisher, even when Forge cannot run the line the piece belongs to.
evidence: Magda, 3 with-lines agent_viability arms: stock picked Portal and the shim overrode it 47/47 times (33 combo-mode, 14 plan-mode); 68/68 across 5 arms. The nocombo arm, with no lines, still overrode 12/12 through plan-mode values 8 over 6.

Plan-piloted Magda 7/48 (15%) vs stock-piloted Magda 47/144 (33%), Fisher p=0.016, lower in all 3 arms. The gap sits in games where Magda's tutor fired: 5/28 vs 43/79 (p=0.0009). Plan Magda fetched Portal from the library 0 times in 72 games.
Portal on the battlefield predicts stock Magda wins, 61/106 vs 5/86. This is confounded (it mostly means Magda came online), so it is not Portal's causal lift.

Finisher regex (unverified): 72/363 value-8 targets are in no line (Pact of Negation in 17/32 decks, Final Fortune, Ragavan). Pact of Negation fetched 33 times, 18 never cast. Plan seats lose to their own spell 8/256 games vs stock 1/768.

Engine tier missing (unverified): early (R1-3) tutors fetched engines 9/18 times for humans, 0/175 for plan seats, 9% for stock. Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora, Esper Sentinel, Necropotence and Seedborn Muse are value 1 in every deck that runs them.

Correction: about 3 in 4 of the 'non-win' steers go to real routes whose outlet is in the deck but that the Forge pilot cannot execute. Fetch class alone barely moves conversion (win-line piece 17% vs non-win piece 15% win within 2 rounds). So the fix is to value pieces by pilotability, not to demote engines wholesale.

plan_feedback.py:196-205 raises finisher-hinted targets by 2 whenever a deck's wins are 70%+ in the combat/life bucket. That is essentially every deck, so once it has data the only learning loop pushes tutors further from combo pieces (store empty locally; production unchecked).
root_causes.already_tried: tasks/20 Stages 0-2 (shim 0.5.0, 2026-08-24..26) added plan-driven search steering. The Portal override was accepted as 'Both are defensible' (tasks/20:139-141). Stage 2 shipped although mean win round moved the wrong way (11.75 -> 13.29). plan_feedback (08-30) added the combat-majority nudge.
root_causes.leverage: Data (Python) plus a data flag read by an existing shim branch. Value pieces by line executability and measured conversion lift from our own logs. Keep a finisher tier for proven closers (Portal-class cards). Restrict combo-mode steer priority to executable win lines via a per-line flag. Add an engine/opener tier that decays after round 3. Drop self-loss and saboteur text from the finisher regex. Disable plan_feedback's combat nudge until the win-method label is fixed.
root_causes.unknowns: No Magda A/B isolates the override from other plan-seat behaviour. Generality: every Portal override is a Magda deck; of the other 7 decks, 2 gain significantly and none loses significantly. The n7 pod's other decks (rog_ishai, selvala) still lose about 11 pp with lines off, for unexplained reasons (plan-mode steering, mulligan and holds all stay on in nocombo).

root_causes.title: The shim's own tutor-cast decision has no model of reach, zone or mode, and fires only when a line is exactly one piece short
symptoms: tutoring: most deliberate combo tutors are spent on a false premise; the piece is often unreachable by type, already in the graveyard, or the tutor never searches at all
tutoring: tutors act as closers, because the only trigger is 'one piece short'
combos: commander-as-tutor opens line pursuit from turn 0 for Magda and Godo and casts pieces early
root_causes.mechanism: lineOfSight treats any plan tutor in hand, or a commander in the command zone (PlanPlayerController.java:1051-1055), as able to fetch any missing piece from any zone (:1063-1070). tutor_cast then casts the first castable plan tutor (:1159-1176) with no check that it can reach the piece. castableSpell hands Forge a raw SpellAbility (:1249-1262), which skips the AI's own target and X choice and casts transmute cards as their spell half. deck_plan.py:113-117 says outright that the tutor list is 'knowingly a little optimistic'.
evidence: Against Forge's own ChangeType restrictions, 316/718 tutor_cast events (44.0%) used a tutor that cannot fetch the sought piece. Forge confirms it: 221 of 222 such casts that resolved a search did not offer the piece.
285/498 (57%) resolved tutor_cast searches could not deliver the piece; 98 casts sought a piece already in the graveyard or exile.

Mode and X failures: 26 casts never reached the stack ('failed to target': Dizzy Spell and Muddle the Mixture cast as spells; Intuition and Gifts with no opponent target). All 18 shim casts of X-cost tutors (Chord, GSZ, Wargate) resolved at X=0, against 17/307 X=0 for stock casts of the same cards.

Commander gate: Magda's command-zone presence opened the gate in 32 of 37 Magda games that were open by turn 4, and was needed for 15/30 Magda combo_casts. Imperial Recruiter and Tezzeret, Cruel Captain were cast 'seeking Helm of the Host' 13 times; neither can fetch it.

Gate shape, corrected for commanders: among plan-seat turns ending with a tutor in hand, 36-41% are two pieces short (55% in rubric_ship) and 42-54% are one short with the gate open but no tutor cast. Decline reasons are not logged; 237/502 eligible turns had a legal, land-affordable tutor that stayed uncast (unverified; tutor keep-weight 5 ties 17-37 cards, strict inequality at :1167-1168).
Scope: tutor_cast decides 419/858 (49%) of plan-seat tutor casts in the cEDH arms, and 0-1 casts per 768 precon games.
root_causes.already_tried: The A18 gate (02e4451, 2026-08-24) is unchanged since. tasks/20 changed what searches pick, not when or whether to cast. Every arm from 0.5.0 to 0.16.0 ran identical tutor-cast logic.
root_causes.leverage: Data plus a thin shim check. deck_plan emits per-tutor reach (types, MV/power/colour caps, destination, mode: spell, ETB, activated, transmute), or the shim tests the piece against the tutor's ChangeZone valid-type through public API. Pieces outside the library count as unreachable. Let Forge's AI finish X and targets, or skip such tutors. Tie commander tutor status to its zone. Log the reason for each decline. Only after reach works, add an opener window as a data dial (for example tutorOpenDistance, or an engine target worth more than the stock pick).
root_causes.unknowns: Why eligible tutors go uncast (weight tie, mana or timing) cannot be told from logs. The win-rate effect of fixing reach is unmeasured. Stock-seat fetch attribution is inferred from zone moves.

root_causes.title: The research system could not see the combo and tutor failures, so two months of work went to combat and timing
symptoms: combos, tutoring and play_logic all persisted because every study was judged on metrics that are blind to them
measurement: 'parity with stock' was read as 'the agent does nothing', when it was +18 pp on Oracle decks and -7 pp on the rest
root_causes.mechanism: Every acceptance gate was pooled win share against stock, correlation with precon humans, behaviour-marker rates or mechanism self-checks. Most games ran on precons, where the combo and tutor code essentially never fired (partly because of a parse bug). No study measured conversion, win round against humans, win method, or whether Forge was willing to play the cards the plan needed. The project correctly concluded on 08-24/08-29 that the gap is conversion and strategy content, then built combat and timing features for the next month.
evidence: 0 of about 10 acceptance gates (tasks 07, 20, 21, 23, engine A/B) measure conversion or win round. The rubric's 76 criteria cover blocking, attacking, interaction and mulligans only.
Pooled parity hides opposite effects: Oracle decks plan 20/96 vs stock 9/288 (+17.7 pp, +4.1 SE); the other six decks 64/288 vs 251/864 (-6.8 pp).

Population: on-disk study corpus 6,135 games; combo- or tutor-focused runs are 452-708 (7-12%). Precon agent arms logged combo_cast 0-4 and tutor_cast 0-1 per 768 games; the 1,536-game overnight ablation logged 2 combo casts and 1 tutor cast.

The only lever that moved win speed toward humans was combo pursuit: 15/93 plan wins by round 6 vs 6/308 stock (p about 2e-6), almost all Oracle. The study read it as a 3.2 pp cost and nearly dropped it.

After 08-29: comboPriority, lineOfSight and tutor_cast untouched; combos.py untouched since 07-31; none of the 1,289 study games run after 08-29 came from a combo or tutor study. Shipped work was 0.10.1 re-aim, 0.14.0 attack targeting, 0.15.0 instant hold and the 0.16.0 combat solver, prompted by the precon backlog, replay callouts and an outside note.
No study measured Forge-side refusals: RemoveDeck, the MAIN2 tutor gate, KeyCards, and setUseSimulation have 0 mentions in the repo.
The human decision corpus was never built: 12 cEDH video games with about 12 expert-labelled decisions, plus 6 midrange tallies. The planned self-recorded capture never happened.
root_causes.already_tried: Nine or more arms (personality dials, hold-back, blockiness, synergy lines, split attacks, 0.15.0 hold, 0.16.0 solver) and the 1,536-game overnight run were all judged on pooled win share or precon correlation. The conversion design was named twice and never tasked.
root_causes.leverage: Product and reporting (Python/harness, no boundary issue). Adopt a combo scorecard for every AI change on combo-live pods: conversion rate by line class, share of wins by round 6 and mean win round against the human 5.0, non-combat combo wins, tutor timing and targets, Forge-refusal rates (flagged cast/activation rate, tutor phase, tutor pick type). Report per deck, stratified by line executability. Build a seeded-board scenario harness. Keep precons for prediction only. Freeze combat work.
root_causes.unknowns: The 12 human games are creator-selected (biased toward fast, exciting games) and several decklists drift, so the true human distribution is unknown. Whether the owner can record 20-30 labelled games is unknown.

root_causes.title: Forge's own tutor AI waits for main phase 2, grabs the best creature, and the data hooks Forge provides to change that are unused
symptoms: tutoring: stock tutors are cast in main phase 2, where most fetched cards cannot be used that turn; upkeep and in-response tutoring (the human pattern) does not happen
tutoring: generic tutors fetch Spirit Guides and big creatures instead of the deck's key cards
root_causes.mechanism: ChangeZoneAi.hiddenOriginCanPlayAI refuses a library-to-hand tutor before MAIN2 unless it is the only card in hand, and refuses library-to-library tutors (Vampiric, Mystical, Worldly, Enlightened, Imperial Seal) before MAIN2 on any turn. Only an ActivationPhases param or AILogic AnyMainPhase changes this, and only Karn the Great Creator sets AnyMainPhase. With no KeyCards set, the chooser falls back to the best creature. Forge has no profile key or AILogic about combos or tutoring, so personality dials cannot reach any of this.
evidence: Bytecode: ChangeZoneAi.hiddenOriginCanPlayAI offsets 946-1056; 'AnyMainPhase' appears only in ChangeZoneAi and only karn_the_great_creator.txt sets it.

Two corpora (runs_016_engine, runs_015_default): stock hand tutors 171/172 in MAIN2 (the exception had hand size 1); stock library-top tutors 263/269 in MAIN2, 0/269 before it. Control: library-to-battlefield tutors take the same path but are exempt, and 292/395 were cast before MAIN2.

Cost: stock hand-tutored cards went unused that turn 51/72. Upkeep library-top casts delivered the card the same turn 10/25 for plan seats, against 1/102 for stock. Off-turn tutor spells: 3-6% in the sim vs 9/29 (31%) for humans.

Correction: plan seats get past the gate on 50-55% of their tutors, yet their mean cast round barely moves (hand tutors 7.2 vs 7.8, library-top 6.0 vs 6.2). So the gate is a within-turn defect, not the main cause of 'closer' behaviour.

Default pick (unverified, from bytecode plus logs): 186/195 (95.4%) of stock generic tutor fetches were creatures (Elvish/Simian Spirit Guide, Nashi, Hullbreaker Horror). The chooser reads Deck.getKeyCards() from .dck [metadata] KeyCards= first. 0 decks write it.
Forge has 0 of 122 AiProps keys and 0 of 344 AILogic values about combos or tutoring; SimLabHuman.ai differs from Default.ai only in two counter chances.
root_causes.already_tried: None. The 0.15.0 instant hold addressed instant-speed answers, not tutors. KeyCards, AnyMainPhase, ActivationPhases and per-card SVars have never been used.
root_causes.leverage: Forge public API and data, zero Java for the first step: write KeyCards= (finisher pieces first) into staged .dck metadata. That also improves stock opponents, so decide deliberately. Then per-instance SpellAbility.putParam('ActivationPhases', ...) on the plan seat's own tutor SAs; AnyMainPhase alone does not clear the library-to-library branch. Then a shim 'tutor window' at an opponent's end step or own upkeep, driven by plan data.
root_causes.unknowns: Side effects of putParam after card construction in ChangeZoneAi's AILogic branches. KeyCards ordering policy, since the list is static and ordered. Whether the gate causes tutors to sit in hand across turns (not measurable without mana data).

root_causes.title: The one line that converts (Consultation + Thassa's Oracle) works through an unintended stack check and also decks its own pilot
symptoms: combos: the only human-speed wins in the whole corpus come from this line, and it self-decks about once for every two wins
play_logic: Thassa's Oracle is cast as a bare creature 53 of 92 times, burning the win condition
root_causes.mechanism: comboPriority's guard `if (!getGame().getStackZone().isEmpty()) return stock;` (PlanPlayerController.java:1094) checks the zone that holds spell cards, not MagicStack, where triggers live. So the shim can cast Consultation while Oracle's ETB trigger is pending, which is the correct human line, even though the commit meant 'only on an empty stack'. The line model has no order and no notion of a spent trigger. The shim casts Oracle early as a 'developing permanent' (:1136), passes stock's own Oracle casts through (:1107), and later counts an Oracle already on the battlefield as a live piece. It then fires Consultation into an empty trigger window and exiles its own library.
evidence: Oracle wins: 25, all plan seats, 0 by stock (stock never casts the flagged Consultation). Median round 6.5 across all 8 run sets (5.0 in the 20-win subset) vs 11.5 for all other wins.

evidence: All unverified by the adversarial pass. Split-moved attackers die for nothing 9.4%, kingmaker moves 7.7%, unmoved 2.8% (precon agent015); cEDH015 moved 9.8% vs 1.0%. Moves are gated only by canAttack (PlanPlayerController.java:536, :748).

counter_fire targets a mana source 73/209 times (Mana Vault 11, Lotus Petal 10, Sol Ring 7); stock spends 20% of counters on mana sources.

Mulligan: 69/228 shipped hands had 1 land or fewer but 3+ mana sources; 0/384 keeps at 5 cards or fewer.

root_causes.already_tried: Most of the two months: personality dials, hold-back, blockiness, split attacks, 0.10.1 re-aim, 0.14.0 attack targeting, 0.15.0 instant hold, 0.16.0 combat solver. root_causes.unknowns: None of these were re-verified. Precision of 'predictable suicide' is estimated at 70-85%. The effect on win rate is likely small given parity; the main value is replay realism and not undoing future combo gains.

measurement_problems: Acceptance metric: pooled plan-vs-stock win share is structurally blind here. It averaged +17.7 pp on Oracle decks and -6.8 pp on the other six into parity. Every agent A/B must report per-deck deltas stratified by line class (spell-completion, activated loop, flagged), conversion rate per assembled line, share of wins by round 6, mean win round against the human 5.0, and win method.

Wrong test bench: most study games ran on precons, where combo_cast and tutor_cast fire 0-4 times per 768 games (partly the |SET suffix parse bug). Use precons only for prediction calibration; judge combo and tutor changes on combo-live cEDH pods. The on-disk corpus is 6,135 games, and combo-focused runs are only 7-12% of it (the '7,671 games / 90%' figure could not be reproduced from disk).

analysis.py 'converted' is correlation, not execution: any win after assembly counts. Of 115 badged rows, 79 (69%) are pure engines whose 153 'conversions' were all combat or life wins, 60% of them a round or more later. product_problems: The results page badges engines 'AI can fire this; results meaningful' (analysis.py:336/352-353, page.tsx:568) when the deck merely won later by any means. The import page (page.tsx:478-479) tells the same user 'the AI assembles combos but rarely fires them'.

'7 of 11 human combo wins lack a complete line': overstated. 3 of 11 are clear line-builder misses (missing outlets); the rest fail on decklist fidelity (Rog/Thras missing Six, Kinnan the wrong build) or have no label (Magda g1). Magda g2's win line is in the plan.
'Stock mean win round ~10.9-11' (human_ceiling RESULTS, brief): Forge turns divided by 4. Winner-own-turn mean is 12.7, so the human gap is about 2.5x.
'Ral never wins in sim because Forge cannot pilot storm': unsupported. Both Ral decks ran without their commander and 6 other cards Forge refused.
'Enable Forge's lookahead as the pilot': the one experiment failed 2/2 (a GameCopier crash, and a timeout with a 361 s single decision). It is viable at most as a bounded line-verification check.
'151 of 168 resource lines have an unused outlet in the deck': not reproducible. An independent list gives 126/168 (107 matched by type).
synthesis.narrative: The AI plays combo decks badly for a few concrete reasons, and none of them is combat or personality, which is where most of the last two months went. First, the combo system gives the AI a shopping list, not instructions: for each deck it passes along every combo Commander Spellbook knows as a bag of card names, and 71% of the 238 cEDH "combos" are engines, like infinite mana or endless triggers, that only win if you also use a finisher the list never names. Second, even when the AI collects every piece, the code treats that as done and hands control back to Forge. The code can only cast spells, never activate abilities or choose targets, so a Kiki-Jiki loop untapped the wrong creature 8 times out of 8, and Derevi untapped Gaea's Cradle 0 times in 216 chances. Of 167 times the AI completed a combo made of permanents, it won that same turn 5 times. Third, Forge's own AI silently refuses to play about one in eight cards in a cEDH deck (cards its authors flagged as "the AI can't play this"), including Demonic Consultation, Vampiric Tutor, Lion's Eye Diamond and Clock of Omens. It refuses them for the opponent seats too, so even the opponents are weaker than their decklists. Tutoring fails in its own ways: tutors are aimed at any combo piece rather than the card that actually wins. The AI's Magda gave up Portal to Phyrexia in all 47 searches where stock Forge would have taken it, and won 15% of games instead of 33%. When the AI decides to tutor for a combo, 44% of the time it picks a tutor that cannot legally find the card it wants, and Forge's own tutor logic waits until the second main phase and usually grabs a creature. The one combo that does work, Thassa's Oracle plus Demonic Consultation, wins around round 5 or 6 like humans do, but it works because of a coding accident, and the same code made the AI exile its own library 14 times. Months of "parity" results hid all of this for two reasons. Most study games used precon decks where the combo code never ran, partly because of a card-name bug. And every change was scored on overall win share, where a gain of about 18 points on Oracle decks and a loss of about 7 on the rest average out to zero. Some study decks were also missing cards: Forge silently dropped 48 double-faced card slots, including the Ral deck's commander, so the conclusion that "Forge can't play storm" was never a fair test. The product then tells users a combo is "AI can fire this; results meaningful" whenever the deck won later by any means, which mostly meant engines that won by combat a round or more later. The order of fixes that follows from the evidence: first fix the measurements (combo conversion rate, per-deck results, a test that starts games with a combo already on the board); then rebuild the combo data so each line names its finisher, order and targets; then add a small step-runner in the shim that plays those steps through Forge's own rules checks; then let the shim re-admit the cards Forge refuses and fix what tutors can reach and when they are cast. Combat tuning should stop until those land. What nobody knows yet is how much win rate a working step-runner buys, and the seeded-board test can answer that cheaply before anything big is built.

verified.root_cause: The plan reads Spellbook's catalogue of engines as a list of wins. Spellbook expects the user to pair an infinite resource with a payoff, and deck_plan has no step that does that pairing.
verified.fix_direction: In deck_plan (Python data), classify each variant's produced features as win or resource. Pair resource lines with an outlet card present in the deck (self-mill to Oracle or Lab Man, mana to Ballista or Thrasios or a commander sink, storm to Grapeshot or Brain Freeze, death triggers to Blood Artist), rank win lines first, and drop or mark bare engines. verification.evidence_rechecked:
I worked from the plans files the shim actually received in studies/behavior_rubric/runs_agent_shipping/plans/plans_*.json, not from a fresh build_plan run. That file set is stronger evidence, and it also avoids plan_feedback.note_tags, which writes to the feedback store.

1) The line counts match exactly: 32 decks, 238 lines. I wrote my own classifier (scratch verify/resource_lines/classify.py). Under a lenient definition of "win" (Win the game; near-infinite damage; infinite hasty tokens; infinite combat phases; infinite power or infinitely large creatures; opponent mill such as Breach + LED + Brain Freeze), I get win 70, resource 168 (71%), and 7 decks with no win line. They are the same 7 the investigator named: derevi 0/10, nadu 0/9, dexter_kinnan 0/4, isaac_yisan 0/29, matt_sisay 0/7, kinnan 0/6, natalie_magda 0/7. Under a strict definition (the literal Spellbook feature "Win the game"), only 17 of 238 lines win and 24 of 32 decks have none. 16 of those 17 lines are Thassa's Oracle + Demonic Consultation, Tainted Pact or Hermit Druid, spread across 8 decks. So the headline is conservative.

2) The code does what the finding says. engine/deck_plan.py:295-301 appends every combos 'included' variant and sorts by len(cards). There is no cap (isaac_yisan ships 29 lines), no produces filter, and no dedupe: 3 exact duplicate piece-sets, for example nadu ships 'Springheart Nantuko + Lotus Cobra' twice. engine/combos.py _slim keeps Spellbook's variants as returned, with no composition step.

3) The shim side is also as described. DeckPlan.java:208 parses only the card names of each line and never reads produces. PlanPlayerController.java:1068 reads `if (onBoard.size() == line.size()) continue; // assembled — done here`. Pursuit is spells-only at lines 1207, 1251, 1294 and 1583 (`!sa.isSpell()`).

4) The Oracle claim holds. Thassa's Oracle is at nadu.dck:92 and appears in no nadu line; it is the only one of the 32 decks with Oracle outside every line. I queried Spellbook /variants for card:"Cephalid Illusionist" card:"Thassa's Oracle" and got 3 results, all needing extra pieces (Grolnok + Lightning Greaves; Nomads en-Kor + Narcomoeba + Dread Return; Flash + Protean Hulk + Nomads). There is no Cephalid + Shuko + Oracle variant.

The human's game-1 turn-5 win (traces/2iA_Jt0d6sM.json) was Chord of Calling for Nadu, then Derevi + Emiel + Gaea's Cradle for infinite mana (that engine IS a plan line), then Blind Obedience plus an Eternal Witness / Snap loop to extort the table. So the plan had the engine and lacked the outlet.

6) Outlet coverage. With my own outlet list (outlets_check.py), 126 of 168 resource lines have an outlet in the deck that no line uses, and 107 of 168 have one matched to the resource type (mana, mill/draw, storm, ETB/death). (a) "removes every ability... never activated". This is true only for voluntary choices. Counterspells, effect-driven casts and mana payment all get past the filter, and stock seats cast flagged cards about 440 times across the studies that way.

(b) "91/235 lines blocked". The accurate figure is 52 for both seat types, or 62 for stock seats. For the 29 mana-ability-only lines (LED, Pili-Pala, KCI, Bloom Tender), I could not attribute the failure to the filter: Forge's AI uses mana abilities only to pay costs, so it would not run those loops regardless of the flag.

(c) "Most cEDH loop engines carry the flag". Wrong: the measured share is 39% of lines.

The mechanism and its evidence are otherwise solid, and the numbers grow when the scan covers all 3,495 study files instead of the investigator's subset.

Why the causal link is 'contributing' and not 'direct'. The flag explains why whole lines are dead:
- the Magda Clock lines (24 deck-lines);
- the ranger, druid and alchemist untap engines;
- Thoracle + Consultation for stock seats. Stock cast Thassa's Oracle in 138 seat-games and won 13 of them, because the Consultation half is never cast.

But 144 of 235 lines contain no flagged piece and still rarely convert. The shim drives no activated abilities for any line and treats an assembled line as done. That is the broader conversion gap, and the flag is one hard sub-cause inside it.

Relevant to the fix direction: when useSimulation is on, chooseSpellAbilityToPlay routes to SpellAbilityPicker, which builds its candidates from ComputerUtilAbility.getSpellAbilities with no RemAIDeck filter. I have not tested whether enabling simulation would then play these pieces sensibly; no simulations were run. A shim override that returns a specific activated SpellAbility would bypass the filter the same way castableSpell does for spells. The repo has never accounted for the flag: a grep of .py/.md/.ts finds nothing. A Python-side 'Forge will not pilot' list built from the card scripts would be cheap.

Caveat on method: I told copies from printed cards by object id (an id that carries another card's name anywhere in the same file is treated as a copy). Card ids stayed stable per seat within each file I inspected, but I did not audit every one of the 78 files that mention Clock.

verification.corrected_claim:
On Magda's own library searches, the plan's search steering overrode stock's pick of Portal to Phyrexia every time in the three with-lines agent_viability arms: 47/47, not 86/86. 33 of those were absolute-priority combo steers to a sighted line's missing piece and 14 were target-value steers (8 over 6). Plan-piloted Magda won 7/48 (15%) against 47/144 (33%) for stock-piloted Magda, p=0.016, lower in all three arms. The gap is concentrated after Magda's search: conditional on activating it, plan won 5/28 against stock's 43/79, p=0.0009.

Portal-on-battlefield predicts a stock Magda win (61/106 vs 5/86), but this mostly measures 'Magda came online'. Stock Portal lands in 74/79 of the games where stock Magda searches, so Portal's own causal value is not isolated.

The steered pieces are not 'never executed'. Forge runs the Magda/Clock Treasure engine to 40-169 Treasures in a turn on wide boards, usually after Portal (20/144 stock games). The plan seat instead assembles a minimal line early (25/48 games) and converts only 4.

In the plan-mode-only nocombo arm the deficit is smaller and not significant (4/16 vs 19/48; conditional on a search, 4/8 vs 18/33). So the harm tracks combo-steer priority plus combo pursuit more than the regex target tiers, and these data cannot separate the override from other combo-pursuit costs.
verification.notes:
All the headline numbers reproduced exactly except the '86/86' in the Quantified line. The investigator's own per-arm evidence sums to 47/47, and 86 seems to be mixed up with the 86 no-Portal stock games.

What I could not verify:
(a) Causal isolation of the override from other plan-seat combo behavior. The plan Magda seats had 30 combo_casts, and holds and instant windows were also active. The clean test is an ablation: the same plan with search steering off, or with Portal pinned at 8.
(b) Generality beyond Magda. Every Portal override in every dataset I checked is a Magda deck, and the other seven decks do not show a plan-seat loss (two show significant gains). This is a strong, deck-specific tutoring failure, not a demonstrated general one.

Adversarial points against the finding:
- The 58%-vs-6% Portal figure is confounded, as noted in the corrected claim, and should not be quoted as Portal's win lift. The conditional-on-search comparison is the defensible evidence.
- The root cause over-weights the oracle-regex target tiers. In the arms where the deficit is measured, the combo path decided 70% of overrides (33/47). In the arm where only target tiers steer (nocombo), the conditional gap disappears, though on n=8.
- The 'fastest observed wins run through the lines' justification in tasks/20:139-141 is contradicted by these data. Plan-seat assembled lines converted 4/25, and the stock seat's big Treasure turns come after Portal, not instead of it.

The finding's fix direction (rank targets by measured conversion, demote combo-steer priority to real win lines) is consistent with what I found. It needs the ablation above before anyone claims it restores win rate.

verification.corrected_claim:
Spellbook lines reach the plan as flat card sets with no notion of what they produce, and the shim drops 'produces' entirely. 173/238 lines (73%) in the 32 cEDH plans have no win effect by the strict text pattern. 'Non-win' does not mean 'dead', though:

- 111 of the 173 (47% of all lines) are one outlet short, and that outlet is already in the deck (Thrasios, Finale of Devastation, Thassa's Oracle, Brain Freeze, Staff of Domination).
- Only about 46/238 (19%) have no known outlet.
The real defect: the plan never names the outlet and gives it target value 1, so the shim steers to it 0 times, and PlanPlayerController.java:1068 treats the engine as done once its pieces are on the board.

Steered fetches that land on non-win pieces: 61-77% in combo mode and 41-67% in plan mode (51-66% pooled per arm), not 55-76%.

Whether a fetch hits a win-line piece barely changes the outcome: 17% vs 15% win within 2 rounds pooled, 18% vs 14% within deck. Assembly is where it shows. An assembled strict-win line converts 31% within 2 rounds (49% of those games won). An assembled outlet-dependent engine converts 9% (26% won). The paper-winning Magda library dump converts 4%. So re-aiming tutors alone will not close much of the gap. The binding constraints are the missing outlet step and Forge not executing loops.

Once a Spellbook line is on the board, the sim rarely wins with it that turn. In agent093 (shim 0.9.3), 31 of the 46 seats that assembled a line lost, and 2 of the 15 winners won on the assembly turn (12 of the 15 by combat). The ban hits things that need no special logic too:
- plain creatures: Bloom Tender 0/32, Devoted Druid 0/24
- mana auras: Utopia Sprawl 0/43
- activated abilities of flagged permanents: the real Clock of Omens was activated 0 times in 83 battlefield entries, while Sculpting Steel copies of it were activated 206 times
- a flagged commander: Winter, Cynical Opportunist is never cast in 120 precon games.

The shim rescues some of these. Its castableSpell checks only canPlay and canPayCost, so it bypasses the filter, but it runs only for spells: plan line pieces and tutors (combo_cast/tutor_cast), plus incidental instant_hold and finisher_hold substitutions (93 of 133 flagged casts on precons). That lifts plan seats to 24.6% cast on cEDH and 5.6% on precons. What changes is the mechanism, and it strengthens the finding and changes the fix. It is one explicit Forge filter, not "no play logic". So:
(a) Many flagged cards (creatures, auras, rocks, and probably some tutors whose per-API logic exists) would likely play correctly if the shim simply re-admitted them. canPlaySa does not consult the flag; only the getSpellAbilityToPlay lambda and saComparator reference isCardRemAIDeck. (b) Re-admitting cards requires the shim to consider non-spell SpellAbilities. castableSpell skips !sa.isSpell(), and that is exactly why assembled lines built on flagged activated engines (Clock of Omens, Devoted Druid, Aphetto Alchemist, Quirion and Scryb Ranger) can never convert.

This is a real measurement bug and I reproduced it exactly, with the suffixed control giving the empty 'C' answer. It falsified a documented claim and led the team to build the synergy-lines fallback on a wrong premise; that fallback's one test predicted worse, with the rank correlation falling from 0.255 to 0.142.

As an explanation of what the owner actually sees, it only contributes. It does not explain the cEDH conversion gap, which is the main complaint that 'combos are wrong'. Those pods use clean names, get 3-29 lines per deck, fire about 100 combo_cast per arm, and still do not convert. It is also not a user-facing bug for normal imports, because convert_decklist writes clean names.

Small product side effects follow from the same parser. A raw Forge .dck with suffixes, uploaded through POST /decks, would show '0 combos' and no 'one card away' suggestion (_deck_combos at mtg_engine.py:979). The deck list would label the commander 'Commodore Guff|CMM|1' (mtg_engine.py:382). And analysis.py:231-232 would report no combos for precon runs, so assembled-vs-converted stats for precons are empty for the same reason. I did not check whether the product ever lists Forge precons to users; no web/engine code references commanderprecons.

'5 precons with win-producing variants' is a judgement call. By the produces text, the clear cases are Counter Blitz and Veloci-Ramp-Tor (damage), Family Matters and Creative Energy (infinite combat), and Goblin Storm or Mind Flayarrgh (mana or storm). Most others give infinite tokens or ETBs and need a payoff.

What is wrong in the finding:

- The 7 cached product analyses in engine/sim_results contain no "fired" rows. I could not check what production users currently see.

- The shim casting Oracle before Consultation is a combo_execution sequencing bug worth its own finding.

Limits:
- Lethal classification uses the last DAMAGE entry within 6 log entries before the LIFE crossing, which is approximate.

verification.notes:
Every key point reproduced. My corrections are about precision, not substance.
- Only 16 of the 18 dropped names come from DFC naming.
- The finding understates the breadth: 48 slots across 23 of 32 decks, not just Ral.
- One of the 7 cards joseph_ral is missing is _____ Goblin, which is not a DFC.
- "2 plan lines" is one line that appears in two pods' plan files.
- The root cause is more specific than "Scryfall-style names": make_dck.py checks names against Forge's script filenames, and those look the same for split cards and DFCs. So PLAN.md:69's promise that card support is checked at conversion was broken for DFCs.

How much this explains the owner's complaint. It is mainly a measurement problem with real product exposure:
- It invalidates 1 of the 8 human_ceiling pod verdicts (Ral storm "never wins").
- It silently weakens 23 of the 32 cEDH decks, often by removing lands (modal cards like Sink into Stupor, Shatterskull and Emeria's Call are lands on the back).
- Any user who pastes a list with 'A // B' names gets those cards silently dropped. Scryfall knows those names, so the import raises no warning.

It does not explain the broad conversion gap. Portal to Phyrexia is not a DFC and it loaded, and the combat-dominated win pattern also holds for the 9 decks with nothing dropped. Only one plan line in all 336 plan files contains a DFC piece. So this is a real contributor to "combos are wrong" and "decks played badly", not the main cause.

Additional product risk, reasoned but not measured. Plan lines take Commander Spellbook's canonical names (combos.py:95). The shim matches exactly against Card.getName(), which returns the face's own name, e.g. "Birgi, God of Storytelling". So a Spellbook combo with a DFC piece would probably fail to match even after the .dck files are fixed. The finding's fix direction already covers this.

What I could not verify:
- Whether Moxfield or Archidekt text exports actually use 'Front // Back' for DFCs (no network).
- That Forge's deck loader skips the card rather than substituting something. The evidence (0 casts, 0 zone records and 93 distinct cards across 30 games) is conclusive in practice, but I did not read the Java code.

Side note: joseph_ral did win 4 of the 22 agent-run games even without its commander. "Never wins in sim" refers only to the 8 stock human_ceiling games.

verification.notes:
What holds up: the line data really lacks outlets and non-infinite finishers, and the Breach loops really cannot be expressed or driven by the shim. The shim half is the stronger evidence, with code line numbers plus a near-zero count of graveyard recasts across every study.

What is overstated: 7 of 11 wins "not complete" becomes 3 clear line-builder misses once you account for decklist fidelity (Rog/Thras is missing Six, Kinnan is the wrong deck), an unlabelled win (Magda g1), and a definition choice (Magda g2 is the human's exact line). The "commander dropped" remark about Ral is not supported: the Ral MDFC is in the plan with role commander and weight 8. The Portal "toolbox" as a required finisher concept is weakly supported: in g1 the creator called that fetch wrong, although the human did fetch Portal again in g2 and won.

Why the causal link is only contributing: several lines that ARE present rarely convert even when assembled. Magda + Clock + Torque won 10 of 32 assembled games, Derevi + Emiel + Cradle 6 of 15, and Nuka-Cola + Manufactor + Grinding never assembled at all. That points to piloting (the shim treats an all-on-board line as "assembled, done here", and has no activated-ability or graveyard-cast drive) as a bottleneck at least as large as missing line content. The proposed acceptance set is reasonable, but 2 of its 11 games rest on decklists known to be wrong or drifted.

verification.corrected_claim:
When a line is one piece short, the shim casts any tutor from plan.tutors that is in hand (PlanPlayerController.java:1159-1176). It never checks whether that tutor can find the missing piece.

It also never checks whether the piece is still in the library: lineOfSight counts graveyard and exile as "outside". And for tutors that work by transmute (Muddle the Mixture, Dizzy Spell, Drift of Phantasms) it casts the spell half instead, because castableSpell accepts only isSpell() abilities.

Across the 447 tutor_casts in the cEDH plan-seat runs:
- 36% cannot match the piece by type, and 45% cannot once fixed cmc, power and colour limits apply.
- A further 16% seek a piece that is in the graveyard, exile or on the stack. Together, 54% (243/447) could not deliver it.
- Only 35-37% delivered the piece within about a round. Reachable casts delivered 67% of the time; unreachable casts 7%.
- The piece was on offer in 41% of the tutor's own searches. For all searches with a named missing piece it was on offer 26-35% of the time, depending on the denominator.

Separately, line 1051 counts a commander in the command zone as a tutor in hand:
- Magda: this is wrong. She searches only from the battlefield by sacrificing 5 Treasures, and once she is on the battlefield she stops counting. The gate is backwards. Her command-zone presence opened the gate in 32 of 37 Magda games open by turn 4, and was needed for 15 of 30 Magda combo_casts.
- Godo: this is right for the Godo + Helm of the Host line, since his enters-the-battlefield search finds Equipment. That line is sighted in 48/48 games purely because of this. It is wrong for his other lines (Basalt Monolith, Rings, Forsaken Monument), where it was needed for 10 of 36 combo_casts.
- The tutor loop never casts from the command zone. So the commander's effect is to cast permanent line pieces early, and to aim tutors in hand at pieces they cannot reach (Imperial Recruiter or Tezzeret, Cruel Captain "seeking Helm of the Host": 13 casts, neither can reach it).

The 74 RemoveDeck:All count is really 109/414 combo_casts. The 76%/80% "cannot execute" figures are unverified.

In precon_predict/runs_agent (768 games) there are 0 tutor_casts, 1 in runs_agent_015 and 1 in engine_ab/runs. So it explains why tutoring fails when the agent tutors for a combo. It does not explain precon tutoring, where the stock AI decides and tutor_steer changes only the search pick. It also does not explain the playtester complaint in tasks/20 ("tutors act as a closer, not an opener"). That comes from the gate design: the loop fires only when a line is exactly one piece short. It is a separate problem from reach.

Beyond what the finding offered, a fix also needs to:
- exclude pieces that are not in the library;
- handle tutors that search by activated ability or transmute (castableSpell casts only spells; Birthing Pod, Tezzeret, Wishclaw and Captain Sisay are cast as permanents, and whether their search ability gets used is left to stock Forge);
- tie the commander's tutor status to whether its tutor effect can happen from its current zone.

verification.notes:
As measurement, the finding's point stands and is stronger than stated. The product KPI in engine/analysis.py counts "converted" as any win after assembly and shows "fired" after a single conversion. On these arms that roughly doubles the true execution count: 64 vs about 25-32 for plan seats. It also counts Oracle-on-board plus a later Consultation as assembled. So the UI can show a combo as fired when the seat actually won by plain combat. Replacing it with an "executed" KPI (spell win, or looped activations or extra combats on the winning turn) is justified.

This contributes to the owner's complaint rather than causing it. Bad measurement does not make decks play badly; it hid where they fail. The project's studies already concluded that lines get assembled but not converted (agent_viability/RESULTS.md:68-74, tutor_targeting/README.md:117). The new parts are the numbers and the product-surface overstatement.

Two things for the orchestrator, beyond the claim:
1. **A concrete combo bug.** comboPriority lets any permanent piece "develop early". For Thassa's Oracle, whose whole value is its enters-the-battlefield trigger, that wastes the card: 6 of 29 shim Oracle casts had no Consultation or Pact that turn, and 7 of the 14 failed Oracle "assemblies" come from exactly this.
2. **Line pursuit hurts some decks.** Plan Magda wins 14.6% vs 32.6% for stock Magda, and plan Nadu 10% vs 20%. Oracle decks gain (Tymna 25% vs 3.5%). The overall parity hides these opposing per-deck effects.

Caveat: the three arms pool shim 0.5.0 (winmax, which has no attach records), 0.15.0 and 0.16.0.

Confirmed: the product defines "converted" as "the seat won at some point after the pieces were on the board together", by any method, with no execution check (analysis.py:336, :353). It then labels any line with one such game "AI can fire this; results meaningful" (page.tsx:568).

- 54 also never won within one own turn of assembly.

Mechanism: Forge's AiController.getSpellAbilityToPlay filters out every ability hosted on an AI:RemoveDeck:All card, for stock seats and shim seats alike. (a) The quoted 376/210 and 42/31 come from the investigator's own zone-based funnel, not from what the product displays. That hides the combo-execution gap the owner is complaining about, and it contradicts the same page's own "Forge's AI does not pilot loops" note.

Second, analysis.py:282 should call board.build(game) so shim runs use the zone read. Without that, the Assembled and From-draws columns undercount on every shim run (the default agent). That second bug is separate from this finding and worth its own task.

- The exact seat-game scope behind the investigator's 211.
- The live production cache (analysis_<file>), which I did not read.

- **A second shim mechanism the finding did not name:** castableSpell hands Forge a raw SpellAbility, which skips the AI's own targeting and X choice.
  - 26 casts never reach the stack ("failed to target"): Dizzy Spell and Muddle the Mixture are tried as their spell half instead of transmute, and Intuition and Gifts Ungiven have no opponent target.
  - All 18 shim casts of X-cost tutors resolve at X=0.
- **Not a shim defect:** 28 casts are countered.

verification.notes:
**Refinements to the finding:**
1. **"No search at all" mixes different causes.** Of the 34 casts of activated-ability tutors, 18 did search on a later turn, outside the one-turn window. Countered casts (28) are not a shim defect. The failed-to-target (26) and X=0 (18) casts come from a separate shim bug: castableSpell substitutes a raw SpellAbility that never gets Forge AI's canPlayAI step, which sets targets and X.
2. **The proposed fix is incomplete.** A search.reach gate would still pass Chord of Calling and Green Sun's Zenith for creature pieces, and they would still resolve at X=0. The same substitution path affects combo_cast and finisherDiscipline: there are 108 "Couldn't add to stack" entries across these arms. The fix also needs the shim to let Forge's AI finish the SpellAbility, setting X and targets through public AI APIs, or to skip X and targeted spells. Transmute needs the ability, not the spell half.
3. **Scope.** This explains bad tutoring on cEDH decks with combo lines, where the shim makes about 49% of tutor decisions. It is irrelevant to precon decks, where tutor_cast fires 0 and 1 times in 768 games per arm.
4. **Impact.** A search that cannot reach the piece still takes something, via the stock pick or a plan steer (e.g. Enlightened Tutor took Esper Sentinel, Mystical Tutor took Ad Nauseam). So the cost is a tutor spent early, plus the stock spell it displaced that window, rather than a blank search. The effect on win rate or conversion is unmeasured.

Small count differences from the investigator (122 vs 123 reachable, exile 6 vs 7, no-search 124 vs 121) come from matching each search_seen once and from the zone-replay cutoff. They do not change the conclusion.

reports.summary: The combo lines the agent chases and the combos the product reports are mostly not win lines, and the Spellbook data that would say so is thrown away on import. combos._slim keeps only card names, a feature list and two text fields. It drops zoneLocations, template requirements, easyPrerequisites and mustBeCommander, and nothing downstream reads the two text fields it keeps. deck_plan then turns every "included" variant into a line with no filter, cap or dedupe. Result on the 32 cEDH pod decks: 168 of 238 lines (71%) produce no win at all (infinite mana, ETB, blink, self-mill), and 7 decks have zero win lines. The outlet that turns the engine into a win (Nadu or Blind Obedience for Derevi, Walking Ballista, Thassa's Oracle) is usually in the deck but in no line. Because every piece gets search value 8, about 60% of tutor steers and tutor casts chase pieces of these non-winning lines. The tutor list carries no type restrictions, so 41% of tutor_cast events cast a tutor that cannot legally find the piece. Zone and order are lost too: Thassa's Oracle is cast early as "development" in 47 of 48 combo casts, and that produced 14 self-decking losses against 25 Oracle wins. Lines needing graveyard casting or activated loops (Breach plus Brain Freeze, Clock of Omens, Emiel) are ones the shim never drives. On measurement: the precon claim that Commander Spellbook returns zero variants is false. It comes from a parser bug (Forge's |SET|art suffix is sent to Spellbook), so every precon arm ran with combo machinery off. In reality 14 of 66 precons have 26 combos and 65 of 66 have almost-included variants. On product: analysis.py calls a combo "converted" and the UI says "AI can fire this; results meaningful" when the seat won by any means, any time later. 96% of those wins were combat. Separately, Forge silently drops cards whose names are written "Front // Back", including the Ral commander and the Birgi combo piece. So the Ral deck that "never wins in sim" was played without its commander.

open_questions: Would win rate move if lines were rebuilt (resource lines composed with outlets, restricted tutors, Oracle ordering fixed)? No simulation was allowed, so all harm figures are mechanism counts, not A/B effects. The agent_viability 'combo pursuit off scores +3.2 pp' result is consistent with these defects but does not isolate them.

Will Forge's base AI execute activation loops (Clock of Omens, Emiel, Crystalline Crawler) if the shim offers the right SpellAbility each priority? Measured: Clock was activated in 9 of 128 games on its own. Whether a thin shim step-driver is enough is untested.

My win-vs-resource split is my own mapping of Spellbook feature names. Borderline features ('Put all artifact cards ... onto the battlefield', non-haste infinite tokens, infinite card draw with Oracle in deck) are near-wins in context, so 71% is an upper bound on 'cannot win' and a lower bound on 'not a win by itself'.
The tutor-legality checker is a regex over oracle clauses (types, MV and toughness caps). The 41% figure could shift by a few points with an exact check against Forge's ChangeType.
The 151/168 'outlet present' count uses a hand-written outlet list and is illustrative. A real composition step should use Spellbook's feature and template graph.
Magda: is steering to Clock or Torque engine pieces over Portal net harmful? The human won once with each route. The evidence of harm is that the base AI almost never runs the Clock loop, not an A/B.
How many user-imported decks carry ' // ' double-faced names Forge drops? The mechanism is proven on study decks; production imports were not inspected.

reports.summary: The combo problem is not a tuning problem. The shim cannot execute almost any of the lines it chases, and chasing them costs games. Of the 235 unique Commander Spellbook lines across the 32 cEDH pod decks, 191 (81%) need an activated-ability step and 176 (75%) do not win by themselves: they make infinite mana or ETBs and need an outlet the plan never carries. The shim does nothing once a line is assembled (PlanPlayerController.java:1068) and only ever casts spells (:1251). On top of that, Forge's own AI never activates any card flagged AI:RemoveDeck:All. That flag sits on a piece of 91 of the 235 lines: the real Clock of Omens had 97 battlefield entries and zero activations. Loops that Forge's generic AI does start stall on a single target choice nobody makes. Across 7 activations, Kiki-Jiki copied Conscripts and the copy's untap never targeted Kiki; Derevi's untap trigger hit Gaea's Cradle in 2 of 2,880 triggers. The one class that works is Demonic Consultation plus Thassa's Oracle. It works by accident: the "empty stack" guard checks the card zone, so the shim can respond to Oracle's trigger. It won 25 games at median round 5.0, the human mean, but it also decked itself 12 times by casting Consultation after Oracle's trigger had already resolved. The reported win-rate parity is the average of two opposite effects. On the two Oracle decks the plan seat is +17.7 pp over stock (+4.1 SE). On the other six decks it is -6.8 pp (-2.4 SE), because casts and tutors are diverted to lines Forge cannot run. The clearest case: plan Magda overrode 47 of 47 searches where stock would have fetched Portal to Phyrexia, stock Magda's main win path (57% win when Portal lands vs 6% without), and fetched mostly Clock of Omens pieces instead. The product then reports these false conversions as "AI can fire this; results meaningful", because analysis.py counts any win after assembly as a conversion.

findings.root_cause: A line crosses the GPL boundary as a bare set of card names. The shim's only verb is 'cast a spell from hand', so 'assembled' is treated as the goal when for 97% of lines it is the starting point.
findings.fix_direction: Send lines as executable scripts (data): ordered steps (cast X, activate Y targeting Z, repeat until condition, then outlet W), zone requirements, prerequisites and a stop condition, compiled on the Python side from the Spellbook description, prerequisites and zoneLocations. The shim becomes an interpreter: return the named SpellAbility (activated abilities included) from chooseSpellAbilityToPlay after canPlay()/canPayCost(), and set the named target. Both are public Forge APIs and the policy stays as data, so this fits the boundary. Until that exists, filter plan lines in deck_plan.py down to the executable classes (a data-only change).

reports.summary: Tutoring fails mainly because of what tutors are told to fetch, not because tutors sit in hand. Since Stage 2 (shim 0.5.0), plan seats cast 76-89% of their tutor spells, and in rounds 1-4 they search at a rate close to humans (0.10-0.16 searches per player-round, against 0.158 for humans). The problem is the aim. 73% of the Spellbook lines in the cEDH plans are engines that do not win on their own (infinite mana, ETB or draw with no outlet). The target scale also gives 8 points to any card whose text says "loses the game" or "combat damage to a player", so Pact of Negation and Ragavan score like combo pieces. Combo steering has absolute priority over everything else. The result: plan-seat steers go 55-76% to pieces of non-win lines. The plan Magda overrides stock's Portal to Phyrexia 100% of the time (86 of 86 in the 3 agent_viability arms). When Portal resolves, stock Magda wins 58% of games; without it, 6%. Plan Magda wins 15% against 33% for stock Magda (p=0.016). The shim's own cast decision (tutor_cast) has not changed since 2026-08-24. It still fires only when a line is exactly one piece short. When a plan seat ends its turn holding a tutor, the best line is two pieces short on 45-60% of those turns (about 60% in rounds 1-4), and 41-49% of shim tutor casts land in round 8 or later. When it does fire, only 29% (123 of 426) of those casts could legally fetch the missing piece: the tutor's type does not match, the piece is in the graveyard or exile, or a transmute card gets cast as its spell side. Forge's own ChangeZoneAi will not cast a tutor to hand, library top or graveyard before main phase 2, on any turn. So stock-cast tutors arrive late, only 3-6% of sim tutor spells are cast off-turn (humans: 31%), and 19-49% of fetched cards are never cast. The playtester complaint is therefore half true. "Every other tutor is plan-blind" is no longer true. "Tutors only act when a line is nearly complete, so they close rather than open" is still true for the shim's decisions. And the new plan targets often point at the wrong card. Finally, the "parity" verdict hides opposite effects by deck. Tutoring toward a real win line (Thassa's Oracle) takes rograkh and tymna from 3% (stock) to 17-25% (plan), and dropping the lines removes the gain entirely. On engine-line decks the same machinery costs win rate.
