findings.claim: When the shim decides to cast a tutor (tutor_cast), the resolved search can legally take the missing piece only 29% of the time.
evidence: miss_reason.py over 426 tutor_cast events (av015, winmax, av016, rubric_ship): piece was a legal option 123 (29%). Tutor type or mana-value restriction excludes it 114 (27%), e.g. Mystical Tutor seeking Thassa's Oracle, Enlightened Tutor seeking Emiel or Felidar Guardian, Summoner's Pact or Natural Order seeking Staff of Domination. Piece in graveyard 34 or exile 7. Piece is a land (Gaea's Cradle) 7. No search at all 121 (28%): activated-ability tutors (Tezzeret, Birthing Pod), transmute cards cast as spells (Muddle the Mixture 10, Dizzy Spell 9), countered.

PlanPlayerController.java:1052-1055: tutorInHand is true for ANY plan tutor. 1069-1070: a line counts as 'clear' with 1 piece outside hand/board/command, including pieces in graveyard or exile. 1159-1176: cast the first castable plan tutor with no reach check. 1249-1262: castableSpell only considers sa.isSpell(), so a transmute card is cast for its spell effect.
findings.quantified: 123/426 (29%) of shim tutor casts could take the sought piece. 27% type mismatch, 10% piece not in library.
findings.root_cause: Line of sight models 'a tutor in hand' as able to find any piece anywhere. Tutor restrictions and the piece's zone are ignored.
findings.fix_direction: Data plus a thin shim change. deck_plan emits search.reach {tutor: [pieces it can legally fetch]} from oracle type/mana-value clauses. The shim gates line-of-sight and tutor_cast on reach and treats graveyard/exile pieces as unreachable. Transmute cards get listed with mode=ability or dropped from tutors. No Forge change.

findings.claim: The shim's tutor-cast decision still fires only when a line is exactly one piece short. The code is unchanged since 2026-08-24. In the early game, most turns that end with a plan tutor in hand are two pieces short, so the shim never opens with a tutor.
evidence: git log -L on PlanPlayerController.java:1047-1085 and 1155-1177: last changed 02e4451 (2026-08-24). Every agent arm since (0.5.0 to 0.16.0) ran identical tutor-cast logic.

gate_state.py, own turns ending with a plan tutor still in hand, best line two short: av015 164/318 (52%), winmax 210/432 (49%), av016 176/392 (45%), rubric_ship 277/461 (60%). Rounds 1-4: 108/180, 114/195, 106/190, 117/185 (about 60%).
A line that is already fully owned also blocks tutor_cast (lineOfSight prefers 0 outside, so missingOutside is null): 5-12% of held turns.
Shim tutor_cast round histogram: round 8+ was 51/125 (41%) av015, 43/104 (41%) winmax, 55/123 (45%) av016, 33/67 (49%) rubric_ship.
findings.quantified: Held-tutor turns two short: 45-60% overall, about 60% in rounds 1-4. Shim tutor casts at round 8+: 41-49%.
findings.root_cause: Stage 5 design rule (1069-1070, 1159): pursuit and tutor casting activate only one piece from completion. Task 20 changed target choice, not the cast decision.
findings.fix_direction: Data dial read by a thin shim change. Allow tutor_cast at two short when a reachable tutor fetches a piece of a WIN line and the other missing piece is also reachable (a second tutor) or is the commander. Gate it per deck in plan JSON (e.g. tutorOpenDistance).

findings.claim: deck_plan's finisher regex gives value 8 (combo-piece tier) to cards whose text only mentions losing the game or combat damage. These false finishers take 13% of plan-mode steers and 20% of the value-8 slots in cEDH plans.
evidence: deck_plan.py:124-125 _FINISHER matches 'loses? the game' and 'combat damage to a player'; deck_plan.py:375-376 assigns val=8.

behavior_rubric/plans_*.json: 72/363 value-8 targets are not in any line and are 8 only via this regex. Examples: Pact of Negation (in 17 of 32 decks), Summoner's Pact, Final Fortune, Last Chance, Warrior's Oath, Angel's Grace, Ragavan, Professional Face-Breaker, Knuckles, Spark Mage.
Plan-mode steers: 67/515 went to these. Pact of Negation 32, overriding Force of Will 12 times and Portal 4 times.
Plan seats fetched Pact of Negation to hand or top 33 times; 18 were never cast.
Precon plans (precon_predict/plans_agent.json): most common value-8 targets are 'combat damage to a player' creatures (Grenzo, Bident of Thassa, Ohran Frostfang).
findings.quantified: 67/515 (13%) plan steers. 72/363 (20%) of value-8 targets. Pact of Negation fetched 33 times, 18 never cast.
findings.root_cause: A cheap keyword regex doubles as the 'finisher' definition. A Pact's upkeep drawback and a saboteur's trigger read as win conditions.
findings.fix_direction: Data (Python): drop 'loses the game' (drawback text) and 'combat damage to a player' from the value-8 tier. Score finishers from real win text or measured conversion.

findings.claim: Forge's ChangeZoneAi forbids casting a tutor to hand (hand size >1), library top, graveyard or exile before main phase 2 on any turn. Stock-cast tutors therefore resolve late, off-turn tutoring is almost absent, and many fetched cards are never cast.
evidence: forge/ai/ability/ChangeZoneAi.class hiddenOriginCanPlayAI, bytecode offsets 945-1056: if phase.isBefore(MAIN2) and no ActivationPhases: CantPlayAi unless destination is Battlefield or Hand, and for Hand when hand size >1 unless AILogic AnyMainPhase.
Stock-seat tutor spell phases (av015, shim 0.15.0): MAIN2 291/426 (68%), MAIN1 101. Plan seats: MAIN1 87, MAIN2 41, DRAW 30, UPKEEP 21 (the shim's tutor_cast bypasses the rule).
Off-turn tutor spells: plan 4%/4%/4%/6%, stock 3-5% (agent_viability, rubric). Humans: 9/29 tutor spells (31%) off-turn (studies/human_ceiling/traces, hand-labeled in scratch human_tutors.json).
Plan-seat fetches to hand/top never cast: 19-49% per arm and decider; 58% of those had 3 or more rounds left in the game. Demonic Consultation 22/37 never cast.
Stock seats strand 22-24% of tutor spells in hand until game end (holds.py); plan seats 4-20%.
findings.quantified: 68% of stock tutor casts in MAIN2. Off-turn 3-6% vs human 31%. Never-cast fetches 19-49%.
findings.root_cause: Base Forge AI timing heuristic. The shim only overrides it through the one-short tutor_cast path.
findings.fix_direction: Thin shim mechanism plus data: a 'tutor window' in chooseSpellAbilityToPlay (public Forge API) that casts a top-of-library or instant tutor at an opponent's end step when the plan names a reachable target. Timing preference stays plan data. No Forge patch.

findings.claim: tutor_cast can only pre-empt a stock choice whose keep-weight is strictly below the tutor's. Tutors are fixed at weight 5 while each cEDH deck has 17-37 other cards at weight 5 or more, so even when a tutor is eligible, the stock pick usually stands.
evidence: PlanPlayerController.java:1167-1168: stockSa == null || weightOf(stock) < weightOf(tutor).
deck_plan.py:343-347: tutors promoted to weight 5. The 'ramp-big-mana' tag (27/32 decks) gives every mana rock and dork enabler weight 5. Commanders are 8.
behavior_rubric/plans_*.json: every deck has 17-37 non-tutor cards at weight >=5 (e.g. derevi 30, nadu 37, rog_ishai 36).

short1.py: of 502 held turns where the best line was one short (tutor_cast eligible), 237 (47%) had a held tutor that could legally fetch the missing piece and lands >= its cmc, yet no tutor was cast.
findings.quantified: Tutor weight 5 ties or loses to 17-37 cards per deck. 237/502 (47%) of eligible held turns had a legal, land-affordable tutor that went uncast.
findings.root_cause: Keep-weights (built for mulligan decisions) are reused as cast priority, with a strict inequality.
findings.fix_direction: Data plus a thin shim change: compare the search-target value of the piece sought, or a plan dial tutorPriority, instead of keep-weight. Log the reason tutor_cast declined so this becomes measurable.

findings.claim: The documented claim that Forge fetches Portal to Phyrexia but never converts it is false in outcome terms. Stock-piloted Magda wins about 10 times more often when Portal resolves.
evidence: studies/tutor_targeting/README.md:61-64 and studies/human_ceiling/RESULTS.md:76 claim Forge never converts.
Pooled stock-piloted Magda (agent_viability stock seats, human_ceiling/runs, tutor_targeting/runs_stock): Portal resolved, 71/117 won (61%). No Portal, 6/91 won (7%).
Win method is mostly combat (Portal strips blockers every upkeep), which is why method-based studies labeled it 'not converted'.
findings.quantified: 61% vs 7% win rate with vs without Portal on the battlefield (n=117 vs 91).
findings.root_cause: Conversion was judged by win METHOD (spell vs combat) instead of by whether the fetched card raised win probability.
findings.fix_direction: Measurement: judge a fetched card's conversion by win-rate lift or ablation, not by method label. Correct the two docs. Observational and confounded by board state; an ablation arm would settle causality.

findings.claim: The tutor regex misses Finale of Devastation (10 of 32 cEDH decks) and land/battle tutors, but it does NOT miss Chord, Green Sun's Zenith, Gamble, Intuition, Mystical, Vampiric or Entomb as the brief suspected. Transmute cards are listed as tutors that tutor_cast cannot actually use.
evidence: census.py over studies/human_ceiling/decks/*/dck (32 decks, 274 tutor copies): regex sees 246. Misses: Finale of Devastation 10 decks (oracle 'search your library and/or graveyard' breaks deck_plan.py:118), Urza's Saga 10 and Inventors' Fair 4 (land-typed, skipped), Invasion of Ikoria 3.
gate_state: Finale held at the end of the seat's own turn 13-34 times per arm without opening the gate.

In plan.tutors but the search is an activated ability or transmute that castableSpell cannot fire: Wishclaw Talisman 6, Kuldotha Forgemaster 4, Tezzeret Cruel Captain 4, Birthing Pod 3, Dizzy Spell 3, Drift of Phantasms 2, Muddle the Mixture 1, and others.
v2_av016.json: 7 tutor_cast events with no zone cast at all (Summoner's Pact 4, Muddle the Mixture 2).
findings.quantified: Finale of Devastation missed in 10/32 decks. 19 tutor_cast events on transmute cards produced no search.
findings.root_cause: _TUTOR_CLAUSE requires 'search your library for' exactly, and skips lands. Tutor listing ignores whether the search is a spell effect.
findings.fix_direction: Data (Python): allow '(?: and/or graveyard)?' in the regex. Tag each tutor with mode (spell/ETB/activated/transmute) so the shim only casts spell/ETB tutors. Stage 2 steering already covers Finale's resolution.

findings.claim: plan_feedback, the only outcome-learning path for tutor targets, nudges finisher-hinted targets up whenever a deck's observed wins are 70% or more combat. Sim wins are almost all combat, so it can only ever push tutors further toward combat cards and never toward line pieces.
evidence: engine/plan_feedback.py:196-203: combat share >= METHOD_MAJORITY raises 'finisher' context targets by 2; spell share >= 0.7 raises line pieces.
engine/mtg_engine.py:263-266: every production run is fed into record_run.
Brief and studies: stock and agent win almost always by combat, so the spell branch essentially never triggers. The local store has 0 games per deck, so no study run was affected.
findings.quantified: One of two branches reachable in practice. 0 study games affected (store empty).
findings.root_cause: Feedback learns from the sim's own combat bias through win-method labels instead of card-level conversion.
findings.fix_direction: Data (Python): replace the method nudge with per-card conversion lift, or leave it off until validated.

findings.claim: No engine or UI code reads search_seen, tutor_steer or tutor_cast. The only tutoring statement a user sees infers tutor efficacy from assembled-vs-draw-odds, which mixes tutors with draw engines and counts non-win engine assemblies as success.
evidence: grep for search_seen|tutor_steer|tutor_cast over engine/*.py, web/lib and web/app: 0 hits.
engine/analysis.py:343-346 and web/app/results/[file]/page.tsx:542 tooltip: 'Assembled above this means tutors did work'.
humanness_scorecard.py, scorecard.py and coach.py contain no tutor timing or target metric; the 'closer vs opener' pattern was never a tracked metric.
findings.quantified: 0 of 3 tutor telemetry events surfaced. 1 heuristic tooltip.
findings.root_cause: Tutor telemetry was built for study analyzers only.
findings.fix_direction: Engine/UI (our side): a per-deck tutor panel showing what each tutor fetched, whether the fetched card was cast, and whether it was a win-line piece. Replace the tooltip claim.

Code reads: PlanPlayerController lineOfSight, comboPriority, castableSpell, rankSearch, targetValue, steer overrides, and git log -L history; deck_plan.py tutor, finisher and target logic; plan_feedback.apply_to_plan; analysis.py combo readings; grep for tutor telemetry in engine and web (none).
Precon plans: only 7 of 66 decks list any tutor; 0-1 decks have lines without synergy. Tutoring is not the precon problem.
open_questions: Causality of the Portal effect: 'Portal on battlefield means a win' is confounded by board state (9 mana). An ablation arm (plan Magda with Portal valued above the line pieces, or engine lines stripped) would settle it, but that needs sims and none were run.
Why eligible one-short tutors go uncast (weight tie vs mana spent vs timing) cannot be told apart from logs. tutor_cast logs no decline reason.
Stock-seat fetched cards are inferred from zone moves (first Library-to-X move by that player in the search's turn, non-land). This can misattribute on multi-search turns; plan-seat values are exact.

Human baseline is small and drifted: 12 games, 45 non-land searches, 4 unknown targets, and list drift documented in manifest.json. The human 'win' label (piece of the line that won) is not identical to the sim's Spellbook win-line definition.

Human vs sim R1-4 shares are confounded by game length (humans end around R5, sims around R11). The per-player-round rate controls for it only partly, because the deck mixes differ (8 human pods vs 2 sim pods).

The per-deck plan-vs-stock split uses the pre-0.16.0 arms, which carry the kingmakerReaim censoring caveat. Deck-level signs are consistent across all three arms, but the magnitudes carry that caveat.

Whether Spellbook 'produces' can reliably separate win lines, and whether its variants carry outlet requirements (e.g. 'requires'), was not checked against the API. The plans only keep 'cards' and 'produces'.

reports.summary: Humans don't win these cEDH pods faster by fighting better. They win because they (a) turn an assembled line into a kill in the same turn, (b) spend early tutors on engines and protection rather than on loose combo pieces, and (c) protect the turn they go off. The sim fails all three, and the logs show it at the decision level. Across the 8 human-ceiling pods, 46 agent seats (0.9.3) assembled a full Spellbook line at a median own round of 7.5. 31 of them lost anyway, and only 2 of the 15 that won did so in the round they assembled. Upper bound: if every assembled line had converted on assembly, the agent's mean win round would drop from 13.1 to 8.8 (stock: 12.7 to 10.2), against a human 5.0. That accounts for about half the gap. The other half is assembly speed. Engines come down at median round 6-8 in the sim versus 4 for humans. Commanders come down about 1 round later (3.0-3.15 vs 2.03). The agent's early tutors fetch combo pieces 57% of the time and engines 0% of the time, where human early tutors went to engines 9 of 18 times. When a combo piece was countered while its caster held a free counterspell, the sim responded 1 time in 39. The root causes are data and mechanism, not dials. First, only 20% of the 235 plan lines include a kill in their "produces" field, and the shim reads only card sets, with no order and no finishing step. Second, 39% of lines include a card that Forge's own scripts flag AI:RemoveDeck:All. Third, deck_plan values draw engines, Seedborn, Gaea's Cradle and free counterspells at 1. The flat "parity" result hides the net of two opposite per-deck effects. The agent lifts Thassa's Oracle decks by 23 pp (p<0.0001) because it can cast spell lines. It lowers activated-loop decks by 13 pp (p=0.02) because it steers them toward loops that neither it nor Forge can run: Magda drops 24 pp, and the plan overrides Forge's Portal to Phyrexia pick 28 of 32 times. Combat, the target of months of work, decided at most 2 of the 12 human games and is the cheapest class on this list.

findings.claim: Once a line is assembled, the sim almost never turns it into a kill in the same turn: 31 of 46 agent seats (0.9.3) that assembled a full Spellbook line lost, and only 2 of the 15 that won did so in the assembly round, while every human loop win was executed on the turn the last piece landed.
evidence: scratchpad/diagnosis/human_vs_sim_decisions/lines.py on studies/behavior_rubric/runs_agent_093 (32 games, 8 pods): 46/128 seats assembled; median own round at assembly 7.5; the game ran a median 5.5 more table rounds; winners' lag median 3, same-round 2/15
Same script on studies/human_ceiling/runs (stock): 25 assembled, 15 won, 13 of those 15 by combat, same-round 1/15, median 3 rounds after assembly
Counterfactual (convert on assembly): agent093 mean win round 13.1 -> 8.8 (20 of 28 decided games faster); stock 12.7 -> 10.2; agentship091 13.8 -> 8.4

Human traces: 10 of 12 wins were loops executed on the assembly turn (Derevi/Emiel/Nadu R5, Cabbage Grinding Station R6, Kinnan->Oracle R4, Font/Clock/Manufactor->Ballista R4, Oboro/Talon Gates R4, Kiki+Conscripts R5, Breach+Brain Freeze R2 and R5, Sisay/Emiel/Deadpool R10, Magda/Torque R6) - studies/human_ceiling/traces/*.json

Only 47 of 235 unique plan lines (20%) include a kill/win clause in 'produces' (e.g. 48 lines lead with 'Infinite creature ETB', 24 with 'Infinite colorless mana'); the shim reads only the card set: simlab-forge-shim/src/simlab/shim/DeckPlan.java:208-213 ('produces' is never read)
PlanPlayerController.java:1068 'if (onBoard.size() == line.size()) continue; // assembled - done here'; :1251 castableSpell 'if (!sa.isSpell()) continue;'

Forge activates engine pieces only a bounded number of times, over 480 games: Emiel up to 11 per turn, Clock of Omens up to 30, Kiki-Jiki 1 per turn (so the Conscripts untap loop never runs), Basalt Monolith up to 5. Grinding Station (106 arrivals), Devoted Druid (14), Transmutation Font (9) and Lion's Eye Diamond (11) were activated 0 times.

Of the loop kills humans used, the only one ever reproduced in 480 sim games is Thassa's Oracle (21 wins). There were 0 Breach/Brain Freeze mill wins despite 33-75 Brain Freeze casts per 32 games, and 0 deck-out losses logged.
findings.quantified: 31/46 assembled agent seats lost (67%); same-round conversion 2/15 agent, 1/15 stock; upper-bound gain 4.3 rounds (agent) / 2.5 rounds (stock) out of an ~8-round human gap
findings.root_cause: The plan data model is card sets with no order, no finishing step and no iteration target. The shim stops pursuing a line once it is on the board, and it substitutes only spells. Forge's AI has no concept of running a loop to its end, so resource engines (infinite mana, ETB, treasures) never reach a kill.
findings.fix_direction: On the Python side, compile each Spellbook variant into an execution script: ordered actions, the finishing step, and when to stop. It crosses as data. In the shim, add a generic interpreter that runs the script through public Forge APIs (activate this SpellAbility on this target, repeat N times, then play the finisher), with Forge still checking legality. That stays a thin adapter because the script is data. Separately, test AiController.setUseSimulation(true) (public) scoped to turns where a line is assembled. Neither needs a Forge patch.

findings.claim: The agent chases and tutors for lines that Forge cannot execute, and on activated-loop decks this makes a strong deck worse. Magda is the human winner of its pod in both games. It wins 16.7% of decided games under the plan pilot against 40.9% under the stock pilot.
evidence: agent_viability runs_015_default + runs_016_engine, per-deck win share of decided games, plan seat vs the same deck as a stock seat: magda 5/30 vs 36/88 (Fisher p=0.025); rog_ishai 8/28 vs 34/90; nadu 4/27 vs 17/83

Magda searches seen by the plan (search_seen src=Magda): stock picked Portal to Phyrexia and the plan overrode it to Adaptive Automaton / Barkform Harvester / Battered Golem in 11/13 (agent093) and 17/19 (av016) cases
Magda activations per seat-game: plan 1.1 (av015: 18 over 16) and 1.2 (av016) against stock 6.6 (316 over 48) and 4.1; stock_hc 6.1, fetching Portal 8 times (the human R3/R4 fetch)

scratchpad aiflags.py over Forge cardsfolder.zip: 91 of 235 unique plan lines (39%) include a card scripted 'AI:RemoveDeck:All' (Clock of Omens in 24 lines, Lion's Eye Diamond in 20, Demonic Consultation 7, Devoted Druid 3, Cephalid Illusionist 2); 57% include some RemoveDeck flag; all 7 natalie_magda lines are flagged
deck_plan.py:295-300 takes every Spellbook 'included' variant with no executability filter; plans_n7WpsqsZtdQ.json values Portal to Phyrexia at 6 ('filler') against 8 for any line piece
findings.quantified: Magda -24 pp (p=0.025); pooled loop decks 20.0% vs 33.3% (p=0.02); Portal overridden 28 of 32 times; 39% of lines contain an AI-unplayable card
findings.root_cause: The plan values any Spellbook line piece at 8 whether or not the pilot can run the line. Tutor steering therefore replaces Forge's sensible toolbox pick with loop pieces, and the line then sits on the board. The loss of Magda activations is observed, but the mechanism behind it is not verified.
findings.fix_direction: Pure data change on our side of the boundary. Have deck_plan.py tag each line as executable or not, from Forge script flags (AI:RemoveDeck, missing AI logic) plus whether the kill needs an outlet the deck lacks. Drop non-executable lines from 'lines', or zero their search values, so Forge's own pick stands. This is also the gate: do it before, or together with, finding 1.

findings.claim: Human early tutors go to engines (draw engines, Seedborn, repeatable tutors) and to interaction. The agent's early tutors never fetch an engine, because deck_plan values those cards at 1 and the shim casts a tutor only when a line is exactly one piece short.
evidence: Human tutors in rounds 1-3 from traces: 9 of 18 fetched engines (Enlightened->Mystic Remora R1, Imperial Seal->Rhystic R1, Worldly->Captain Sisay R2, Finale/GSZ/Nature's Rhythm->Seedborn Muse R3 x3, Worldly->Metamorph-as-Seedborn R3, Worldly->Peregrin Took R3, Vampiric->Rhystic R2); across all 44 named human tutors, 12 went to engines and 7 to interaction
scratchpad tutor.py, early (R1-3) tutor casts: plan seats 175, of which 57% combo piece, 0 engine, 0 interaction; stock seats 300, of which 9% engine, 3% interaction, 34% 'other'

Plan search targets: Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora, Esper Sentinel and Necropotence = 1 'filler' in every deck that runs them (25 decks). Seedborn Muse = 1 in kinnan, rog_thrasios, cabbage_merchant x2 and alan_tnt. Captain Sisay = 1. Collector Ouphe = 1. Lands are skipped entirely at deck_plan.py:373, so Gaea's Cradle, the Sisay/Crop Rotation target, cannot be valued.
PlanPlayerController.java:1159 tutor_cast only when 'sight.missingOutside != null' (one piece short): the agent treats tutors as closers

Stock premium tutors (Demonic, Vampiric, Imperial Seal, Grim, Mystical, Worldly, Enlightened, Gamble, Wishclaw, Diabolic Intent): 67/447 (15%) fetched Simian or Elvish Spirit Guide. rograkh_silas stock fetched Nashi 48 times; derevi stock fetched Volatile Stormdrake 38+ times.

Human expert-labeled tutor errors are all about the target class: Magda Portal 'objectively incorrect' (n7 g1), Finale for a 2-drop instead of Collector Ouphe (n7 g2), Vampiric for Rhystic instead of free interaction (sZA, 'game-losing'), Demonic Tutor for Remora instead of Oracle (B421)
findings.quantified: Early tutors fetching engines: human 50% (9/18), plan 0% (0/175), stock 9% (26/300); plan values draw engines at 1 in 25 of 25 decks
findings.root_cause: deck_plan.py's search-target scale has no engine or opener tier. It skips lands and labels most free counterspells 'enabler'. The shim's tutor trigger is structurally a closer. Stock Forge's own tutor evaluation prefers cheap creatures such as the Spirit Guides.
findings.fix_direction: Data: in deck_plan.py add an 'engine' role, with values for card-advantage and tempo engines and repeatable tutors, carrying an 'opener' context (value high before round 3, decaying after), mirroring the existing ramp/beforeRound hint. Allow legendary and combo lands as targets. Shim (thin): let tutor_cast fire when an opener target in the library is worth more than the stock pick, not only when a line is one piece short. The policy stays in Python.

findings.claim: When the sim's combo piece or commander is countered while its caster holds a free counterspell (Force of Will, Pact of Negation, Fierce Guardianship, Deflecting Swat, Mental Misstep), it fights back 1 time in 39. Humans pushed about half of their wins through with protection.
evidence: scratchpad protect_free.py (STACK_RESOLVE 'X - Counter Y' plus the caster's hand rebuilt from the zone stream): held free protection and responded: agent093 1 of 13, agentship091 0 of 9, av015 plan 0 of 3, av016 plan 0 of 3, stock 0 of 11

findings.root_cause: No policy of the form 'go off only with backup, and spend the backup on your own win'. The role labels that could drive one are wrong, and Forge's counter AI only fires in response to threats against the table.

Replace the random greed roll with a data rule: hold the finishing piece while opponents have open counter mana and I have no protection, otherwise go.

findings.claim: Thassa's Oracle is usually cast as a bare creature, which burns the win condition. Stock does this in 59 of 65 casts and never won with Oracle. The shim itself sequences Oracle before the exile spell, because it treats every permanent piece as something to develop early.
evidence: scratchpad oracle2.py, Oracle casts with no Demonic Consultation or Tainted Pact available: stock_hc 8 of 9, av015 stock seats 28 of 28, av016 stock seats 23 of 28, all with 0 Oracle wins; plan seats 4 of 17 (av015), 9 of 19 (av016), 9 of 14 (agent093)
Agent combo_cast events: 'Thassa's Oracle (0/2 online)' x29, meaning Oracle is cast first as a developing piece; 'Demonic Consultation (1/2 online)' x32, of which 18 won that turn and 14 did not
PlanPlayerController.java:1136 'if (!c.isPermanent() && !completes) continue;' lets a permanent piece be cast before the line completes, which is wrong for ETB-payoff pieces
findings.quantified: Stock burns Oracle in 91% of casts (59/65) with 0 wins; plan burns 22/50, and 14/32 post-Oracle Consultations fail
findings.root_cause: The line model has no ordering. ETB-trigger payoffs (Oracle) must come after, or in response to, the exile spell. The stock AI has no hold discipline for win-condition creatures.
findings.fix_direction: Data: an order or 'fire_last' flag per line piece, emitted by deck_plan.py (Oracle and Laboratory Maniac-style pieces are ETB payoffs). Shim: cast a fire_last permanent only in the same priority window as the exile spell, and never when the exile spell is neither in hand nor castable. This is a generic rule that reads data.

reports.summary: Outside combat dials, the biggest error I found is card coverage, and no study in the repo measures it. Forge's own card scripts mark 2,551 cards "AI:RemoveDeck:All", meaning its AI cannot play them. Those cards are 12.1% of the nonland cards in the 32 cEDH pod decks and 4.7% in the 66-precon cohort. When one reaches a stock seat's hand, stock casts it 4.6-8.1% of the time on cEDH (versus about 70% for other cards) and 1.0% on precons; 63-81% of them sit in hand until the game ends. The dead cards include the heart of cEDH combo and tutoring: stock cast Vampiric Tutor 0/28 times, Demonic Consultation 0/32, Ad Nauseam 0/49, Lion's Eye Diamond 0/86, Culling the Weak 0/44, Praetor's Grasp 0/38 and Summoner's Pact 0/40. Two unflagged free interaction spells also go uncast: Deflecting Swat 0/82 and Mindbreak Trap 0/109. The shim's combo_cast and tutor_cast raise the plan seat to about 24% on flagged cards, which fixes some line pieces and tutors but leaves most of them dead. Stock Forge also wastes rituals: 30% of classic rituals and 62% of Jeska's Will casts on cEDH are followed by nothing. Every one of the 51 wasted-ritual cases I checked had an AI-blind card in hand, which suggests Forge's ritual lookahead counts a follow-up spell the AI then refuses to cast (inferred, not verified in Forge source). Stock also discards combo pieces and tutors at cleanup (0.27 per cEDH seat-game) and spends free counterspells on mana rocks (20% of its counters). The shim adds two errors of its own. First, its split and kingmaker re-aim passes move attackers with only a legality check, and moved attackers die for nothing 3-4x as often as unmoved ones. Second, voluntary chumps (chumpiness 0.15, plus the 0.16.0 solver) cost 2-8x more needless chump blocks per seat-game than stock. Each of those two costs more creatures, in absolute terms, than the headline free-block gain recovers, which fits the repeated win-rate parity. Missed land drops (about 1.6-2.5% of turns), unspent mana while holding a castable permanent (about 10% of precon turns, half of it AI-blind cards), self-kills and dying while holding a saver are all low-rate and equal between pilots, so they come from stock Forge.

findings.claim: Forge's AI casts almost none of the cards its own scripts flag AI:RemoveDeck:All: 12.1% of cEDH pod nonland cards and 4.7% of precon nonland cards are flagged, stock casts 4.6-8.1% of them on cEDH versus about 70% of unflagged cards, and 1.0% versus 76% on precons.

findings.quantified: cEDH stock: 2.31 flagged cards reach hand per seat-game (887/384) and about 95% are never cast. Stock pooled cast rate 5.6% of 2,139, plan 24.2% of 574. Precons: 0.79 per seat-game, 99% never cast.
findings.root_cause: Forge's per-card AI logic has no play logic for these cards (tutors to the top of the library, Pacts, LED, Doomsday-style cards, redirect spells, filter rocks). The shim only forces casts through comboPriority/castableSpell for cards in plan lines or tutor lists, and only under line-proximity gates, so everything else stays dead.
findings.fix_direction: Data side (legal): generate an 'AI-blind' list per deck on the Python side from Forge's RemoveDeck flags plus measured per-card cast rates from existing runs, and ship it in the plan. Give each card a cast-policy entry (window, preconditions, target preference) and have the shim execute it through the existing castableSpell/canPlaySa path, which uses public Forge APIs. Cards that need Forge-side targeting logic (Misdirection, Deflecting Swat, Mindbreak Trap) cannot be fixed by the shim; disclose them instead. Upstream PRs to Card-Forge for the tutor cards are the other legal route.

findings.quantified: Moved attackers die for nothing 7.7-9.8% versus 1.0-2.8% unmoved. That is about +0.09 to +0.15 extra predictable suicide attackers per plan seat-game (precon mixed 0.24 vs 0.15; cEDH015 0.27 vs 0.15).
findings.root_cause: Forge's AiAttackController picks each attacker's defender with that defender's blockers in mind. The shim reassigns defenders by threat score alone and never re-evaluates blocks, so it feeds bodies into boards Forge had deliberately avoided. Introduced by the shim, not inherited from stock.
findings.fix_direction: Thin shim mechanism plus data: apply the hasUntappedBlockerFor / blockerWouldBeDestroyed test that preferOpenTarget already uses to split and kingmaker moves (skip a move that sends an attacker into a profitable block), or set splitAttacks to 0 in deck_plan.py. Both are within the legal boundary.

findings.quantified: Classic rituals: 30% wasted (40/134) for stock and 37% (23/63) for plan on cEDH. About 0.11-0.13 wasted rituals per cEDH seat-game for both pilots. Precon stock 8/46 classic.
findings.root_cause: Inherited from stock. Most likely (inferred from the 51/51 association, not verified in source) the ritual logic counts a follow-up spell as castable with the added mana, and then that follow-up's own play decision refuses it (AI-blind cards), so the mana empties.
findings.fix_direction: Thin shim gate using public APIs: when the stock pick is a ritual (list supplied by Python as data), allow it only if some other hand card passes getAi().canPlaySa == WillPlay and can be paid with the ritual's mana; otherwise veto the pick. Rituals inside a plan line keep going through comboPriority.

findings.claim: Plan seats make chump blocks at high life when the incoming attack is not remotely lethal 2-8x as often per seat-game as stock, and this absolute cost is larger than the headline free-block gain.

Neutral RubricObserver block records (life before >= 20 and incoming power <= half of life), per seat-game: cedh015 plan 0.297 vs stock 0.089; cedh016 (0.16.0 seeBlocks solver) plan 0.633 vs stock 0.078; overnight base mixed precons plan 0.268 vs stock 0.173; precon agent015 1178 over 3072 seat-games = 0.38
Per block made: cEDH015+016 plan 119/457 = 26% vs stock 64/1088 = 5.9%

findings.claim: Both pilots spend counterspells, many of them free or pitch counters, on mana sources: stock 20% of counters and plan 25%. On the plan side, 35% of the agent's 'fired' counters target mana sources, because its threat list is built from keep-weights.
evidence: counters.py: cEDH stock 136/677 counters aimed at mana sources (cedh015 61/286, cedh016 53/282, hc_stock 22/109), 101 of them with Force of Will/Negation, Fierce Guardianship, Pact of Negation, Mental Misstep or Daze; plan 66/264, 47 free or pitch

Quoted pairs: stock 'Pact of Negation' on Chrome Mox and Arcane Signet, 'Fierce Guardianship' on Fellwar Stone, 'Force of Will' on Selvala; plan 'Force of Will' on Basalt Monolith, 'Pact of Negation' on Delighted Halfling

findings.quantified: Stock 20% (136/677), plan 25% (66/264) of counters on mana sources; 35% (73/209) of agent counter_fire events. This refutes 'fired counters aim at win attempts' as written.
findings.root_cause: Stock: Forge's counter AI has no threat model beyond CMC and chance settings. Plan: keep-weight (what I want in my opening hand) is reused as threat to the table, so opponents' fast mana scores 8, and the SimLabHuman profile makes stock want to counter every 1-2 CMC spell.
findings.fix_direction: Data only: build the threat list separately from keep-weights in deck_plan.py; exclude mana sources and rituals unless the card completes a visible line (the line_completion_seen logic already exists); consider dropping the SimLabHuman CMC overrides, which skill_headtohead found do no measurable work (A-D +0.34 pp).

findings.claim: About 10% of stock combat eliminations on cEDH pods (15/153) happen while the dying player holds an instant that removes, bounces or fogs the single attacker whose removal would have saved them, with the mana to cast it. Plan seats: 3/51 on cEDH, 5/480 on precons.

A naive version counting any held counter or removal flagged 31-43% of all cEDH eliminations; most of those were Mental Misstep or Pact of Negation held against combat damage, which is irrelevant

findings.root_cause: Inherited from stock: the AI does not look for a lethal-preventing response in declare blockers.

Verified turn alignment: 16/16 land plays match between the LAND entries and zone Hand->Battlefield records.

Validated the MANA-entry tapped-land estimator against exact tap records on precon agent015: 10.2% estimated vs 9.7% exact 'unspent castable permanent' turns, 2.18 vs 2.14 mean untapped lands. Land MANA entries cover 250/256 land taps.

Datasets: cedh015 and cedh016 (128 games each, 1 plan vs 3 stock seats), cedh_shipping (32), human_ceiling stock (32), precon runs_stock (766), runs_agent_015 (768), overnight base mixed pods (512), engine_ab (128).
Missed land drop detector (all datasets, phaseless rule for apples-to-apples): about 1.6-1.7% of player-turns, stock equals plan; cross-checked against shim hold events (5/300 coincide).

End-step unspent mana with a castable non-flash non-Aura permanent (colour-aware bipartite payability): about 10% of precon turns for both pilots; 52-58% of sampled cases involve only RemoveDeck:All cards.

Died holding a saver: the naive version (31-43% of cEDH eliminations) was rejected after inspection (irrelevant counterspells); the refined combat-only, one-removal-saves version gives 15/153 stock and 3/51 plan.

Attackers dying for nothing (blocked, died at a damage step, killed no blocker) plus a predictable-from-printed-P/T subset; attribution to shim move events (attrib.py): split 9.4%, kingmaker 7.7%, open_reaim 1.0%, no move 2.8% on precons.
RubricObserver chump analysis per seat-game; free-block accounting shows the agent's block edge is about 0.05 blocks per seat-game.
Counterspell target classification (counters.py) and counter_fire threat audit (73/209 on mana sources); traced to deck_plan.py:430 and the SimLabHuman.ai CMC overrides.

Removal on own permanents: 0.4-4% of targeted removal (low). Removal on a 2-or-less-power creature while a 7+ power enemy stood: 1.3-5% (low). Wrath while the caster has the biggest board: 5-9% of wraths, both pilots (low, noisy); fixed an early bug where the wrath's own effects were counted.

Forge AI flag index built from cardsfolder.zip (34,216 scripts); deck composition for 32 cEDH and 66 precon decks; per-card cast table for 43 key cEDH cards; correlation of flagged share with the precon sim-minus-human residual (-0.16, p=0.21, n.s.).
Generic tutors fetching lands on plan seats: 7/105 search_seen (6 of them Beseech the Mirror); left to the tutoring dimension.
Not run: simulations (none allowed); 'spells cast into obvious counter mana' and 'commander recast with no board' were not built as detectors.
open_questions: Is the wasted-ritual mechanism really ManaAi.doManaRitualLogic counting a follow-up the AI then refuses? The evidence is the 51/51 association only; decompiling ManaAi.doManaRitualLogic and AiController.canPlaySa would confirm it.

If the shim force-casts AI-blind cards through castableSpell, does Forge make sane choices for their sub-decisions (Culling the Weak's sacrifice, Praetor's Grasp's target, LED's discard)? Those choosers may be just as blind; this needs a small targeted sim to check.

How much win rate or conversion do the dead cards cost? Seat-level analysis is confounded by deck identity and game length; a paired A/B that swaps AI-blind cards for AI-playable equivalents would answer it.

Predictable-suicide precision is limited by P/T recorded at battlefield entry (anthems, counters and pumps are not tracked live) and by intentional death triggers (Reassembling Skeleton, Pests); I estimate 70-85% precision from sampled examples but did not hand-label a sample.
The human traces carry no normative-error codes, so there is no human rate for wasted rituals, suicide attacks or dead cards; the standards applied here are normative, not comparative.

Pre-0.16.0 plan runs carry the kingmakerReaim re-ask contamination; the attack-attribution numbers come from the first declaration only (the shim leaves re-asks untouched), but censoring still differs by arm.

reports.summary: Forge's own AI code has three hardcoded behaviours that cause most of the "combos wrong, tutors bad" symptoms. Nothing the agent arms tested ever touched them, so those arms were bound to land at parity. (1) AiController.getSpellAbilityToPlay drops every spell or ability whose card script says `AI:RemoveDeck:All`, and the sort comparator gives those cards -10 priority. That flag covers 11.2% of cEDH deck cards and at least one piece in 38% of plan combo lines. Measured: stock seats cast 5.2% of flagged cards they draw, against 62.9% of unflagged ones, and they activate flagged permanents 1.5% of the time against 52%. Plan seats get only partial rescue (12-21%) because the shim substitutes spells only. (2) ChangeZoneAi.hiddenOriginCanPlayAI refuses any tutor to hand before main phase 2 while the hand holds more than 1 card, and refuses tutors to the top of the library before main phase 2 at all. Stock seats cast 76/77 hand tutors and 120/123 library-top tutors in MAIN2. This is the "tutors act as a closer" complaint, and it comes straight from Forge code. (3) With no key cards set, a generic tutor fetches the best creature: 186/195 stock picks (95.4%) were creatures, mostly Spirit Guides and big bodies. Forge already reads an ordered `KeyCards=` list from the .dck metadata first, and nobody in the project writes one. Forge has no combo concept anywhere: 344 AILogic values, no combo/tutor/sequencing profile property, and SimLabHuman.ai differs from Default only in two counter chances. So profile dials cannot produce combo play. Forge's lookahead (AIOption.USE_SIMULATION / setUseSimulation) does see activated abilities and flagged cards and picks tutor targets by search. But I enabled it in a scratch shim copy and it failed in both games: one crashed on turn 13 (GameCopier "Couldn't map Goblin Token"), and one timed out at 915 s after 26 turns, with 585 s spent inside simulation (one decision took 361 s) and 2 game-copy errors. Its material-only evaluator (depth 3, stack not copied) also passed over the combo commander. The usable levers are data and thin mechanisms: KeyCards metadata; re-admitting flagged cards through the public AiController.canPlaySa; per-card hint injection through the public Card.setSVar / SpellAbility.putParam; activated-ability pursuit in the shim; and GameSimulator as a bounded check that a planned line really finishes, not as the pilot.

findings.claim: Forge's stock main-priority AI removes every spell/ability whose host card is flagged `AI:RemoveDeck:All` from its candidate list, so decks' flagged combo pieces, tutors and even Signets are essentially never cast or activated by stock seats and only partly rescued on plan seats.

CardRules$Reader: 'RemoveDeck' + 'All' -> removedFromAIDecks (javap line 564-575). SpellAbilityPicker has no RemAIDeck check (simulation candidates are unfiltered)

findings.quantified: cEDH stock seats cast 178/3430 (5.2%) of drawn flagged cards vs 11045/17567 (62.9%) unflagged. Flagged cards are 13.2% of drawn nonland cards. 91/238 (38.2%) of cEDH plan lines contain a flagged piece. Precons carry 4.86 flagged cards per deck (median 5, max 11)
findings.root_cause: Forge authors flag cards their per-API heuristics cannot play, and AiController then refuses to consider them at all (Forge's GUI warns about this via complainCardsCantPlayWell, which is skipped only when simulation is on). The cEDH combo and tutor staples are exactly the cards Forge flags.
findings.fix_direction: Thin shim mechanism plus data: after super.chooseSpellAbilityToPlay(), collect the plan seat's SAs whose host is flagged AND named in plan data (deck_plan.py can compute the flagged list by reading res/cardsfolder/cardsfolder.zip, or emit an explicit readmit list). Evaluate each with the public getAi().canPlaySa(sa), which does not apply the flag filter, and include non-mana activated abilities, not just isSpell(). Take the SA when the decision is WillPlay and its plan weight beats the stock pick. Do NOT edit card scripts in res/ (that modifies Forge's distribution). Measure with the flagged-card cast rate from scripts/castrate.py. Stock opponents stay unaffected unless the product wants realistic opponents too.

findings.claim: Forge's tutor AI refuses to cast a library-to-hand tutor before main phase 2 whenever the hand holds more than one card, and refuses a library-to-library tutor (Vampiric, Mystical, Worldly) before main phase 2 at all. That is why stock tutors act as closers.
evidence: ChangeZoneAi.hiddenOriginCanPlayAI offsets 945-1056 (dump ChangeZoneAi.txt lines 560-1038): if phase.isBefore(MAIN2) and there is no ActivationPhases param, a destination that is neither Battlefield nor Hand returns CantPlayAi. If hand.size() > 1 and the destination is Hand and AILogic != 'AnyMainPhase', it also returns CantPlayAi. Only playImmediately() bypasses this
scripts/tutorphase.py on runs_016_engine (the only corpus with phase recorded): stock tutor-to-hand casts 76/77 in MAIN2 (1 in MAIN1). Stock library-top tutors 120/123 MAIN2, 3 END_OF_TURN
Same corpus, plan seats: hand tutors cast before MAIN2 in 26/45 (57.8%), library-top 31/61 (50.8%). The shim's tutor_cast overrides the rule only when a line is one piece short
Demonic Tutor script comment in cardsfolder.zip: 'TODO: Improve the tutoring logic for the AI'
findings.quantified: Stock seats cast 196/200 (98%) of hand and library-top tutors in MAIN2, where the fetched card usually cannot be used until the next turn
findings.root_cause: A hardcoded timing heuristic in Forge's generic ChangeZone AI. It has no notion of tutoring as an opener or of a combo line, and AnyMainPhase is an opt-in AILogic that no cEDH tutor script sets.
findings.fix_direction: Two data-driven options inside the boundary: (a) at game start, the shim calls the public SpellAbility.putParam("AILogic","AnyMainPhase") on the plan seat's own tutor SAs, using a list from deck_plan.py. This is a per-instance hint and Forge code stays unpatched. It is untested, so check for side effects in the AILogic branches of chooseCardToHiddenOriginChangeZone. (b) Widen the shim's tutor_cast from 'exactly one piece short' to a plan-data opener policy. Measure: pre-MAIN2 tutor share, and tutored card cast the same turn.

findings.claim: With no deck key cards set, Forge's generic tutor fetches the best creature in the library. Forge already reads an ordered KeyCards list from .dck metadata that overrides this choice, and the project never writes one.
evidence: ChangeZoneAi.chooseCardToHiddenOriginChangeZone offsets 9-208: key card = first entry of player.getRegisteredPlayer().getDeck().getKeyCards() present in the fetch list and not already in hand or on the battlefield. It is returned at offsets 828-835 (creature search), 896-903 (battlefield/graveyard) and 949-956 (hand/library), BEFORE the fallback
Fallback, offsets 1047-1067: getNotType(Land) -> filter CREATURES -> chooseCreature. Only when there are no creatures: life>5 sortByCmcDesc castable, else getBestAI
DeckFileHeader/DeckSerializer: metadata keys 'KeyCards' (';'-separated) and 'AiHints'. SimShim loads decks via DeckSerializer.fromFile + RegisteredPlayer.forCommander, so the list reaches the game

scripts/tutorpick.py (tutorpick.txt): stock generic tutor-to-hand picks were creatures 44/46 (016), 60/61 (015), 61/64 (winmax), 21/24 (human_ceiling). Top picks: Elvish/Simian Spirit Guide, Nashi, Hullbreaker Horror, Kuldotha Forgemaster. Thassa's Oracle 10/195
grep over the repo and shim for KeyCards/getKeyCards/addKeyCard: 0 hits
findings.quantified: 186/195 (95.4%) of stock generic tutor fetches were creatures. KeyCards used by 0 of 32 cEDH decks and 0 bundled decks
findings.root_cause: Forge's generic tutor target logic is 'best creature' (the source TODO admits it). The one data hook Forge provides (Deck key cards) was never discovered.
findings.fix_direction: Pure data, zero Java: have deck_plan/convert_decklist write `KeyCards=Piece A;Piece B;...` (finisher pieces first) into the [metadata] section of the staged .dck. This improves stock opponents' tutoring too. For situational choice, the shim can call the public Deck.addKeyCard/removeKeyCard as the missing line piece changes. Caveat: the list is static and ordered, and the plan seat's own steerSearch still overrides it. Measure the tutor pick-type distribution and fetch-to-conversion rate.

findings.claim: Forge's AI has no combo, tutor or win-sequencing knowledge that any profile or card-script data can switch on, so the personality and profile arms could not have produced combo play.
evidence: AiProps enum: 122 keys (javap forge.ai.AiProps). The only sequencing-related ones are PRIORITY_REDUCTION_FOR_STORM_SPELLS, MIN_COUNT_FOR_STORM_SPELLS, PREDICT_SPELLS_FOR_MAIN2, RESERVE_MANA_FOR_MAIN2_CHANCE, PLAY_AGGRO. There is no combo or tutor key
diff Default.ai SimLabHuman.ai: only CHANCE_TO_COUNTER_CMC_1/2 differ (30/75 -> 100)
cardsfolder.zip: 344 distinct AILogic values over 1,990 uses. None match combo|win|loop|infinite|tutor|storm
forge/ai/*.class string scan for 'combo': only mana 'comboColors', SpecialCardAi$Intuition 'donateComboMightWin', and ChangeZoneAi 'saheeliFelidarCombo' (two hardcoded special cases)
AiCardMemory$MemorySet has 13 sets (attackers, held mana, bounced, and so on), none for combo pieces
findings.quantified: 0 of 122 profile keys and 0 of 344 AILogic values address combos or tutoring. 2 hardcoded combo special cases in all of forge.ai
findings.root_cause: Forge's AI is a per-card, per-API heuristic engine that evaluates each spell in isolation. A multi-card line exists nowhere in its model.
findings.fix_direction: Stop spending on profile/dial arms for conversion. Combo policy has to be ours (Python plan -> data -> shim executes), which is already the legal posture. Forge can only supply legality (canPlay/canPayCost/canPlaySa) and, narrowly, lookahead verification.

findings.root_cause: The simulator is an experimental GUI-only feature: a brute-force depth-3 material search with fragile game copying (tokens and stack not reliably mapped). It has never been hardened for 4-player Commander, and its evaluator does not know what a combo is.
findings.fix_direction: Do not enable it as the default pilot. The durable lever is its public pieces: new GameSimulator(SimulationController, game, player, phase).simulateSpellAbility(sa) plus getSimulatedGameState(). Use them as a bounded oracle in narrow windows (own main phase, empty stack, a line in sight): 'if I play this piece or activation sequence, is the game over or the line converted?'. Wrap in try/catch for GameCopier RuntimeExceptions and set a time budget. The success criterion comes from plan data. That stays a thin shim mechanism. Changing MAX_DEPTH needs reflection, so avoid it.

reports.summary: Two months of studies have not fixed combos or tutoring because almost none of the work was aimed at them, and the metrics used to judge the work cannot see them. About 90% of simulated study games (6,917 of 7,671) ran on precons. Commander Spellbook has zero combo lines for those decks, so the combo and tutor machinery barely ran there: 2 combo casts and 1 tutor cast in the 1,536-game overnight ablation. Every "parity" verdict built on those games says nothing about combos or tutoring. The project decided on 2026-08-24, 08-25 and 08-26 that the binding gap is CONVERSION, meaning actually executing a combo once its pieces are down. It never wrote a line of conversion code. After the last combo change (0.9.3, 2026-08-29), the next four AI changes were attack targeting, finisher holds, an instant-speed hold and a combat solver. Two of them came from an outside architecture note and from a precon-prediction backlog. In the shim, a fully assembled line is skipped as "assembled, done here", and only spells are ever cast. The plan hands over each line as a plain set of card names. Spellbook's step text is cached on disk by combos.py and thrown away twice before it reaches the shim. I measured what no study measured. On cEDH pods the plan seat assembles a combo made only of permanents twice as often as stock (37.9% vs 18.5% of seat-games). It then wins within one round of assembly only 4.1% of the time, against 14.5% for stock. Lines that need activated abilities (Unctus+Aphetto, Staff+Selvala, Druid+Reconfiguration, Breach+Grinding Station) converted 0 of 30 times. Combo pursuit is the ONLY intervention that ever moved the human-relevant metric: 16% of plan-seat wins came by round 6, against 2% for stock (p about 2e-6), almost all of them Thassa's Oracle spell lines. The study read it as a 3.2 pp win-rate cost and nearly dropped it. Several documented numbers are wrong: the human-ceiling rounds are Forge turns divided by 4 (the true stock mean is 12.7 rounds, not 10.9), and more than half of agent clock-censoring was the re-ask loop bug, not slow deliberation.

reports.summary: The product's combo and play-quality surfaces send wrong signals of their own, on top of whatever the AI gets wrong. I ran the product's own analysis.py over 320 adapted cEDH games across 4 study arms. It gave 107 distinct combo rows the badge "AI can fire this; results meaningful". 99 of those (93%) are infinite-mana, ETB or lock engines that cannot win by themselves. The badge only means the combo's owner won the game somehow after the pieces had been on the battlefield together. In 116 of 199 of those conversions the win came at least a full round later, and 195 of 199 were by combat. Only the Thassa's Oracle lines were real combo kills. analysis.py also works out "Assembled" from stdout inference even when the exact shim zone stream is present. The replay uses the zone stream, so the replay and the combo table disagree. Example: the table says Clock of Omens was "never available in 62 of 64 games" and that the Magda line never assembled, while the zone stream shows Magda tutoring it onto the battlefield and the line assembled in 15 games. The win-method label "combat damage / life loss" is shown as "by combat damage". On the newest product run, the game-ending blow was a drain or non-combat kill in 7 of 15 games labelled that way, and it absorbs a genuine Sanguine Bond loop kill. The same label feeds plan_feedback, which in production would push tutor targets toward finishers for any deck that "wins by combat" (almost every deck). That is a direct route to the playtester report that "tutors act as a closer". No surface shows tutor decisions, the deck's plan, or misplays. The agent's search, steer, combo and hold events reach the replay payload and are never rendered. The replay shows an Oracle deck exiling its own library and then losing to an empty library draw, and nothing flags it. The "Win-condition telemetry" page scores charge counters and proliferate at table level for every deck. The scorecards measure only combat, mulligans and land drops, which nine study arms showed are not where win rate lives. The UI never says which pilot played, stock or plan agent. A validity bug labels a deliberate all-stock run "Mixed pod" and drops it from the leaderboard.
